8WNMUNJfub.key_idea: Search ancestor-closed draft subtrees using expected committed tokens divided by cycle time, charging nodes only for newly activated experts.
8WNMUNJfub.evidence: The excerpts report CNN/DailyMail summarization and evaluation across multiple GPUs and expert-cache capacities.
8WNMUNJfub.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the analysis of the trade-off between speculative acceptance and expert-transfer cost and the reported baseline improvements.
8WNMUNJfub.main_concern: Multiple reviewers question deployment feasibility because the evaluated routing atlas uses expert activations obtained ahead of inference.

E2nid6vm0N.one_liner: Network-aware expert localization, replica balancing, and predictive prefetching reduce multi-node communication in MoE serving.
E2nid6vm0N.problem: Serving large Mixture-of-Experts models across multi-node clusters suffers from slow cross-node communication and GPU load imbalance because existing redundant-expert placement methods ignore hierarchical network topology.
E2nid6vm0N.method: Albus pairs expert-locality-enhanced routing with communication-aware load balancing to optimize redundant expert placement across intra-node and inter-node links. Its runtime integrates predictive scheduling and expert-replica prefetching with reusable execution buffers.
E2nid6vm0N.key_idea: Combine locality-enhanced routing and topology-aware expert replica placement with predictive scheduling and prefetching across hierarchical multi-node networks.
E2nid6vm0N.evidence: System throughput, load balancing, and accuracy evaluations are conducted on GLM-4.7 and DeepSeek-R1 across multi-node deployments.
E2nid6vm0N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree Albus presents a coherent, well-motivated system design that coordinates topology-aware placement, predictive preparation, and load balancing for multi-node MoE inference.
E2nid6vm0N.main_concern: Reviewers note incremental novelty relative to predictive MoE serving systems like Libra and LPLB and express concern that approximate locality-boosted routing makes model accuracy deployment-dependent.

dno6Q1iEEG.one_liner: An SE(3)-invariant structure encoder and Transformer set decoder jointly predict protein domain masks and fold labels.
dno6Q1iEEG.problem: Sequential two-stage pipelines for protein domain parsing and fold classification cannot optimize both coupled tasks jointly and propagate boundary-parsing errors into fold assignment.
dno6Q1iEEG.method: The authors construct TEDBench-Joint from The Encyclopedia of Domains and propose DoTR, an end-to-end SE(3)-invariant 3D residue encoder with a Transformer set decoder that jointly predicts an unordered set of domain residue masks and fold classes.
dno6Q1iEEG.key_idea: Encode 3D residue structure with an SE(3)-invariant backbone and decode an unordered set of domain residue masks and fold classes jointly.
dno6Q1iEEG.evidence: Experiments on TEDBench-Joint compare DoTR against dedicated domain-parsing baselines and sequential parsing-plus-classification pipelines on fold-agnostic and fold-aware metrics.
dno6Q1iEEG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying protein domain segmentation and fold classification in the large-scale TEDBench-Joint benchmark with an end-to-end baseline addresses a clear gap in structure annotation.
dno6Q1iEEG.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about evaluation circularity and label noise in TED's automated consensus annotations, missing main-text evaluation criteria, and DoTR's inability to identify unseen folds.

qQrxQuOdhC.one_liner: Structured artifact lists act as explicit video-quality rubrics, trained jointly with preference scores through multiple rewards.
qQrxQuOdhC.problem: Opaque scalar rewards and unconstrained rationales provide limited evidence for video-quality judgments.
qQrxQuOdhC.method: ArtiVidRM first lists visible video artifacts and then scores quality using those rubrics. Multi-reward reinforcement learning supervises artifact coverage and efficiency together with pairwise preference ranking.
qQrxQuOdhC.key_idea: Joint artifact-prediction and preference rewards train an observe-then-score model with a structured defect list as an intermediate representation.
qQrxQuOdhC.evidence: Preference benchmarks, component ablations, expert checks, and Wan and Veo generation applications evaluate the reward model.
qQrxQuOdhC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see structured defect descriptions as interpretable, potentially actionable feedback and appreciate the varied evaluations.
qQrxQuOdhC.main_concern: No intervention establishes that the predicted artifact list actually determines the quality score rather than serving as a post-hoc rationale.

X5fdHev0al.one_liner: A landmark-selecting manager and action-generating worker learn separately with width-based search to solve larger planning instances.
X5fdHev0al.problem: General planning policies face longer plans and growing decision costs as problem instances scale.
X5fdHev0al.method: Landmarker trains a manager to select atomic landmark subgoals with reinforcement learning while search achieves them. A separately trained worker learns from search-generated plans and replaces search at deployment.
X5fdHev0al.key_idea: Width-based search trains landmark ordering and primitive-action execution separately before a learned worker substitutes for search.
X5fdHev0al.evidence: IPC 2023 learning-track experiments compare learned heuristics, learned policies, and LAMA, including random-subgoal-selector ablations.
X5fdHev0al.claimed_gains: Landmarker solves 648 of the 900 test instances, compared with 668 for the strongest lookahead policy.
X5fdHev0al.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find landmark-based decomposition well motivated and recognize generalization to large planning instances.
X5fdHev0al.main_concern: Unequal hardware and resource limits, together with excluded landmark-extraction time, undermine fair efficiency comparisons.

scDDtMm52e.one_liner: Caption verification, rare-condition expansion, and reinforcement learning iteratively generate supervision for instruction-following speech synthesis.
scDDtMm52e.problem: Missing or inaccurate speech attributes in captions limit the controllability learned by instruction-following TTS systems.
scDDtMm52e.method: IterCap selects self-generated captions using acoustic checks and independent caption models, expands underrepresented delivery conditions through controlled audio editing, and retrains iteratively. Multiple-choice verification with GSPO optimizes caption correctness.
scDDtMm52e.key_idea: Verified self-generated captions and edited speech examples feed iterative training, with reference-anchored multiple-choice rewards supervising caption attributes.
scDDtMm52e.evidence: Caption-accuracy evaluation and fixed-backbone downstream comparisons test whether changing caption sources improves instruction-following TTS.
scDDtMm52e.claimed_gains: IterCap raises macro-averaged per-dimension caption accuracy to 83.4%, compared with 75.3%.
scDDtMm52e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the caption-quality problem and controlled downstream evidence that improved captions benefit TTS instruction following.
scDDtMm52e.main_concern: The caption-verification process lacks sufficient independent validation, particularly for edited target attributes and shared model biases.

DFBebstNto.one_liner: Answer-flip lookahead selects findings by decision value to allocate reading, computation, and stopping.
DFBebstNto.problem: Confidence can fail to indicate correctness when a model lacks the information needed to answer.
DFBebstNto.method: The training-free, gold-free criterion evaluates findings by their likelihood of changing the model's greedy answer. A controller uses this decision value to select information and govern computation and stopping.
DFBebstNto.key_idea: Candidate-finding lookahead measures changes to the greedy answer instead of entropy reduction or confidence gain.
DFBebstNto.evidence: Interactive MedQA-USMLE experiments compare self-consistency, information revelation, confidence-gated computation, reading controls, and calibration-dependent selection behavior.
DFBebstNto.claimed_gains: At low information, 16× self-consistency gains +0.017 (p=0.72), while revealing two findings gains +0.197 (p<2×10^-4).
DFBebstNto.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers recognize the distinction between missing information and insufficient computation and find decision changes a useful alternative signal.
DFBebstNto.main_concern: Comparisons do not isolate decision-value selection from the advantage of accessing additional findings and the cost of probing their contents.

0TErtW2wFc.one_liner: Residual-driven NTK spectral dynamics model how weight decay sustains feature learning after training accuracy saturates.
0TErtW2wFc.problem: Grokking requires explaining delayed generalization after early memorization as learning leaves a fixed-kernel regime.
0TErtW2wFc.method: For homogeneous networks with squared loss and L2 decay, the analysis derives persistent residuals and projects coupled kernel dynamics onto task-relevant spectral directions. A reduced system balances residual-driven kernel growth against weight decay.
0TErtW2wFc.key_idea: Persistent residuals, especially in small-eigenvalue directions, drive task-aligned NTK growth that competes with weight decay.
0TErtW2wFc.evidence: Modular-addition experiments on homogeneous MLPs and Transformers compare learning-rate and weight-decay sweeps with predicted spectral dynamics and phase behavior.
0TErtW2wFc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the coupled residual-kernel analysis and systematic tests of its quantitative predictions.
0TErtW2wFc.main_concern: The theoretical results do not establish how the analyzed kernel dynamics produce generalization or its delay relative to training fit.

ifnqPJaf0e.one_liner: Recovery dynamics, hidden-state readability, and lightweight repair jointly classify recoverability of post-training capability loss.
ifnqPJaf0e.problem: Equal performance drops can reflect either hard-to-elicit retained capabilities or losses requiring substantial relearning.
ifnqPJaf0e.method: TRIAGE combines recovery behavior, hidden-state readability, and lightweight-repair operability into a continuous Forgetting Typing Score. The score guides repair choices for suppression-like versus overwrite-like losses.
ifnqPJaf0e.key_idea: A fused recoverability score combines representation readability and intervention responses to route forgotten capabilities toward suitable repair procedures.
ifnqPJaf0e.evidence: Leave-one-injection-type-out evaluation, transfer tests, matched RLVR/SFT comparisons, and a controlled 2×2 study assess diagnosis and repair.
ifnqPJaf0e.claimed_gains: FTS achieves 0.921 AUROC, and FTS-guided repair reaches a common ≈90% recovery target at 1.7–2.4× lower cost than uniform replay.
ifnqPJaf0e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing capability loss by recoverability and using that distinction to choose repair interventions.
ifnqPJaf0e.main_concern: Evidence for practical benefit remains limited by the tested repair settings and modest added value over simpler repair heuristics.

MUpw6kgkXl.one_liner: Conditional flow matching jointly reconstructs metric hand and camera trajectories from egocentric video in a shared world frame.
MUpw6kgkXl.problem: Separate hand and camera estimates propagate errors, while monocular scale ambiguity and occlusion make motion reconstruction uncertain.
MUpw6kgkXl.method: DewHand combines VGGT-Ω scene geometry with hand-specific features and metric supervision to predict hand and camera motion jointly. Conditional flow matching represents plausible trajectories under occlusion.
MUpw6kgkXl.key_idea: Joint hand-camera flow generation combines scene geometry, articulation features, and metric supervision in a shared world coordinate system.
MUpw6kgkXl.evidence: HOT3D and ARCTIC experiments compare world-space accuracy and temporal consistency, with camera-supervision and direct-regression ablations.
MUpw6kgkXl.claimed_gains: DewHand reduces rigid-aligned world-space error relative to StableHand from 32.9 to 28.4 mm.
MUpw6kgkXl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize substantial metric-scale and world-space reconstruction gains and useful camera-supervision evidence.
MUpw6kgkXl.main_concern: Fixed five-second offline windows limit applicability to long videos, with stitching and boundary behavior insufficiently addressed.

HigeKZlLM7.one_liner: Matched prerequisite probes and research-workflow inspection test whether fluid-mechanics knowledge translates into problem solving and scientific execution.
HigeKZlLM7.problem: Scientific benchmarks usually assess knowledge, application, and research execution separately rather than testing their connection.
HigeKZlLM7.method: FluidBench combines textbook-grounded questions, multistage application problems with prerequisite probes, and open-ended research tasks. A six-dimensional diagnostic framework and workspace inspection characterize failures.
HigeKZlLM7.key_idea: Matched knowledge probes accompany application problems, while artifact inspection evaluates whether agents sustain valid end-to-end research workflows.
HigeKZlLM7.evidence: Evaluation includes 625 foundational problems, 329 multistage application problems, and 10 open-ended tasks across five research topics.
HigeKZlLM7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the knowledge-to-action question and the linked, multilevel diagnostic benchmark.
HigeKZlLM7.main_concern: Heavy dependence on LLM judgments lacks sufficient expert calibration and independent validation of research scores and failure labels.

m1ayD7h5Ji.one_liner: Reviewer-derived concern categories require source evidence, bounded absence certificates, or reproducible computations for survey-quality criticism.
m1ayD7h5Ji.problem: Opaque LLM verdicts and heuristic metrics make literature-survey quality assessment difficult to verify.
m1ayD7h5Ji.method: SurveyAudit derives the ConTax concern taxonomy from real reviews and applies category-specific detection procedures. Every detected concern must carry a source span, bounded absence certificate, or reproducible computation path.
m1ayD7h5Ji.key_idea: Category-specific concern detectors attach inspectable evidence traces to criticisms grounded in a taxonomy derived from human reviews.
m1ayD7h5Ji.evidence: The taxonomy uses 519 reviews of 168 surveys, and experiments evaluate human-written, AI-generated, and controlled-perturbation surveys.
m1ayD7h5Ji.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value connecting real reviewer concerns to explicit, inspectable detection criteria and evidence requirements.
m1ayD7h5Ji.main_concern: Evidence traceability does not establish that cited material meaningfully supports the detected concern.

Kd80NWKxvG.one_liner: A shared tensor transform, local residual prediction, and Half thresholding estimate corruption while retaining signal beyond low-rank references.
Kd80NWKxvG.problem: Low-rank restoration can discard genuine fine-scale signal that lies outside a compact reference representation.
Kd80NWKxvG.method: ST-HalfNet learns an orthogonal transform and nonuniform slice ranks under a total budget, then estimates a low-rank reference with scaled factor updates. Local regression corrects omitted signal before Half thresholding estimates corruption for subtraction from the observation.
Kd80NWKxvG.key_idea: Predicting genuine signal omitted by a low-rank reference corrects the residual before Half thresholding isolates sparse corruption.
Kd80NWKxvG.evidence: Rank-allocation and restoration-error analysis accompany full-resolution CAVE and ICVL experiments with salt-and-pepper corruption and unchanged-weight transfer to other sparse corruptions.
Kd80NWKxvG.claimed_gains: ST-HalfNet exceeds the strongest baseline by 2.94 to 13.14 dB in transfer settings.
Kd80NWKxvG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize strong CAVE and ICVL results and the value of preserving observed detail outside the low-rank reference.
Kd80NWKxvG.main_concern: Real-image ablations do not isolate learned-transform benefits from those of nonuniform rank allocation.

KSMfeUR4AY.one_liner: Multi-turn reinforcement learning trains teachers against simulated student archetypes using their post-tutoring performance.
KSMfeUR4AY.problem: Successful problem solving does not guarantee effective teaching, and generic pedagogical supervision may ignore individual student outcomes.
KSMfeUR4AY.method: Sherpa instantiates LLM students with different learning preferences and trains a teacher through multi-turn interactions. Student outcomes provide the learning signal for adapting instructional behavior.
KSMfeUR4AY.key_idea: Preference-conditioned student archetypes interact with a teacher whose multi-turn reinforcement-learning reward measures post-tutoring student performance.
KSMfeUR4AY.evidence: Automated archetype evaluations, MathTutorBench, human pairwise judgments, and transfer to unseen student types and models assess teaching.
KSMfeUR4AY.claimed_gains: Student performance improves by an average of 20.5 percentage points, MathTutorBench pedagogy rises from 52.5% to 79.2%, and humans prefer Sherpa in 79.6% of pairwise comparisons.
KSMfeUR4AY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find outcome-based tutor training well motivated and recognize gains across simulated students and evaluations.
KSMfeUR4AY.main_concern: Explicit preference requests and gate feedback make it unclear whether the teacher infers student needs or simply follows disclosed strategies.

dQpf9tCRag.one_liner: A Designer agent recursively generates task worlds whose concepts build on earlier worlds to test conceptual bootstrapping.
dQpf9tCRag.problem: Independent or fixed intelligence tests cannot measure sustained acquisition of new concepts from previously learned ones.
dQpf9tCRag.method: ARC-infinity repeatedly extends a seed world through a Designer agent, separating conceptual direction from implementation. Two hyperparameters control growth depth and breadth, while library learning consolidates prior knowledge for evaluated agents.
dQpf9tCRag.key_idea: Generate each new task world by composing concepts established in earlier worlds, producing a recursively expanding evaluation sequence.
dQpf9tCRag.evidence: Generator ablations test component choices and growth controls, and agent evaluations along a generated worldline compare bootstrapping with and without library learning.
dQpf9tCRag.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value evaluating cumulative concept acquisition and the separation of conceptual planning from task implementation.
dQpf9tCRag.main_concern: Insufficient verification of task solvability and conceptual dependencies undermines the validity of measured bootstrapping failures.

PC2gPgG5Ts.one_liner: Risk-supervised latent rollouts predict safety margins and collision probabilities for receding-horizon crowd navigation.
PC2gPgG5Ts.problem: Reactive navigation cannot explicitly evaluate action-dependent futures, while trajectory-based planning becomes expensive as crowds grow.
PC2gPgG5Ts.method: RiskNav rolls out action-conditioned latent states from observation history and a local waypoint. A risk evaluator supervises the encoder and predictor with safety margins and collision probabilities, which enter a horizon-wise planning objective.
PC2gPgG5Ts.key_idea: Backpropagate explicit safety-risk losses through latent rollouts and use the predicted risks to score candidate action sequences.
PC2gPgG5Ts.evidence: Indoor, open, and out-of-distribution evaluations compare nine baselines using paired episodes, with representation-shaping and planning-risk ablations.
PC2gPgG5Ts.claimed_gains: RiskNav reports strict success rates of 0.76, 0.57, and 0.50 in indoor, open, and out-of-distribution settings, respectively, the highest among nine baselines.
PC2gPgG5Ts.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value safety-informed latent planning and its practical computational benefits for crowded scenes.
PC2gPgG5Ts.main_concern: The main pedestrian setting ignores robot actions, limiting evidence that the model predicts action-dependent human-robot interactions.

3EoH49TYLt.one_liner: Prefix- and depth-causal conditioning overlaps parallel drafting with target verification while layer looping refines speculative tokens.
3EoH49TYLt.problem: Target-latent-conditioned drafters normally wait for verification, leaving drafting latency on the decoding critical path.
3EoH49TYLt.method: PaPaSpec restricts each drafter layer to target latents already computed, allowing drafting and verification to run concurrently. Intermediate drafter layers loop until fresh target conditioning arrives to refine drafts without increasing model size.
3EoH49TYLt.key_idea: Expose only available target latents to each drafter layer and loop intermediate layers while concurrent verification produces new conditioning.
3EoH49TYLt.evidence: Single-request H100 experiments cover seven math, coding, and chat benchmarks, with ablations of intermediate-state conditioning and layer looping.
3EoH49TYLt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that causal access to intermediate target states offers a technically motivated way to overlap drafting and verification.
3EoH49TYLt.main_concern: Using a dedicated additional GPU for the drafter makes baseline comparisons and the practical value of the latency gains uncertain.

MiIx6Dukj2.one_liner: Hint-free distillation coupled with autonomous reinforcement learning trains coding agents to retain useful guidance after hints disappear.
MiIx6Dukj2.problem: Verified coding successes can depend on privileged guidance and fail to transfer to independent problem solving.
MiIx6Dukj2.method: HTC-RL first distills mixed autonomous, hint-assisted, and teacher trajectories under hint-free contexts. Continued training combines reinforcement learning on unhinted rollouts with hint-free online distillation of successful hinted rollouts.
MiIx6Dukj2.key_idea: Train on successful hinted trajectories under hint-free contexts while retaining policy-gradient updates from autonomous rollouts.
MiIx6Dukj2.evidence: A 9B coding agent undergoes terminal and repository-repair experiments, including privileged-channel controls, held-out evaluation, and comparison with plain RL from the same distilled initialization.
MiIx6Dukj2.claimed_gains: HTC-RL scores 28.1 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 57.2 on SWE-bench Verified, gains of 4.5 and 6.4 points over Stage 0, and solves 16 versus 6 of 197 terminal tasks absent from initial demonstrations but included in continued training.
MiIx6Dukj2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing guided success from independent coding capability and examining privileged-information dependence.
MiIx6Dukj2.main_concern: The method's distinction from existing hint-assisted distillation and joint reinforcement-learning approaches lacks sufficient explanation and comparison.

fkLFVABijT.one_liner: Ordered remote-history and current-sentence coupling trajectories distinguish machine-generated documents from human writing.
fkLFVABijT.problem: Static document representations and aggregated statistics miss how remote discourse history contributes to writing as a document unfolds.
fkLFVABijT.method: PEC-Detector encodes remote history and local context separately, then relates them to each current sentence. Ordered coupling representations drive document classification, while conditional semantic prediction trains the remote-history state to retain execution-relevant information.
fkLFVABijT.key_idea: Model the ordered trajectory of remote-history contributions to current-sentence prediction beyond immediate local context.
fkLFVABijT.evidence: Public benchmarks cover multiple domains, generators, and languages, alongside an independent conditional-prediction analysis trained without source labels.
fkLFVABijT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find remote history's conditional contribution a useful, testable source of document-level detection evidence.
fkLFVABijT.main_concern: The interpretation of remote-history features as discourse planning lacks evidence separating planning from topic continuity, repetition, or other textual regularities.

TfnRRmsIRj.one_liner: Cached value predictions supply task-progress memory while online reinforcement learning adapts robot policies from deployment experience.
TfnRRmsIRj.problem: Partial observability makes robot actions ambiguous, and offline post-training delays learning from deployment feedback.
TfnRRmsIRj.method: Value as Memory conditions the policy on recent value predictions and transitions from offline RL warmup to sparse-reward autonomous online learning. Updates combine demonstrations, off-policy interventions, and on-policy rollouts, with concurrent collection and training.
TfnRRmsIRj.key_idea: Feed recent critic predictions into the action policy as a temporal memory of task progress.
TfnRRmsIRj.evidence: Real-world long-horizon deformable-object and contact-rich manipulation tasks compare caching ablations, matched offline training, recovery behavior, and online training schedules.
TfnRRmsIRj.claimed_gains: VaM reports a mean absolute success-rate gain of 29.4% with value caching and a 32.8% gain with online autonomous learning, with 8× as many policy iterations at the same gradient-step budget and more than 2× lower recorded time per gradient step.
TfnRRmsIRj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value using recent value estimates as practical memory and the consistent gains on difficult physical manipulation tasks.
TfnRRmsIRj.main_concern: The ablations do not isolate value-specific progress information from extra temporal context, additional inputs, or model capacity.

fEtkAPkvSO.one_liner: Autoregressively generate explicit image coordinate sequences in VLMs trained with a Fréchet-based geometric RL reward.
fEtkAPkvSO.problem: Vision-language models struggle on connectivity and curve-tracing visual reasoning tasks when connectivity cannot be inferred from direct visual cues.
fEtkAPkvSO.method: Chain-of-Coordinates (CoC) trains VLMs to autoregressively output sequences of image coordinates as intermediate reasoning traces using a two-stage reinforcement learning framework with a continuous Fréchet-based geometric reward.
fEtkAPkvSO.key_idea: Represent intermediate visual reasoning as autoregressive text coordinate sequences optimized via reinforcement learning with a sampling-invariant continuous Fréchet trajectory reward.
fEtkAPkvSO.evidence: Supported by theoretical analysis of representability, learnability, geometric approximation error, and circuit complexity, plus empirical evaluation across six curve-tracing and connectivity tasks.
fEtkAPkvSO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicit coordinate traces provide a unified, tool-free geometric representation paired naturally with a sampling-invariant Fréchet reward and rigorous theoretical analysis.
fEtkAPkvSO.main_concern: Empirical evaluation is restricted to stylized synthetic curve-tracing tasks on very small single-seed test sets without isolating coordinate representation gains from extra trajectory supervision and RL.

1iRPOgchOG.one_liner: Decompose multimodal in-context learning into readout-subspace signal power and head-alignment readability to test visual concept induction.
1iRPOgchOG.problem: Existing multimodal in-context learning evaluations confound genuine visual concept induction with the recognition of familiar semantic associations.
1iRPOgchOG.method: The authors evaluate MLLMs in a controlled multi-attribute classification setting and decompose final-layer representations into signal power within the frozen language head's subspace and readability measuring alignment with the readout head, supplemented by linear probing and LEACE interventions.
1iRPOgchOG.key_idea: Decompose final-layer query representations into readout-subspace signal power and readout-alignment readability to test whether in-context demonstrations create new concept information or steer existing features.
1iRPOgchOG.evidence: Evaluated on a synthetic four-attribute dataset (Clevr-4: color, shape, count, texture) using behavioral accuracy, linear probing, geometric decomposition, and LEACE causal interventions.
1iRPOgchOG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled multi-attribute setup and readout-frame decomposition provide a clear perspective on how in-context demonstrations steer existing features and induce competing-attribute interference.
1iRPOgchOG.main_concern: Because probes are retrained per condition on already-familiar visual attributes present in every query image, stable probe accuracy does not conclusively prove the claim that demonstrations only read rather than write information.

2KvSYrWwH6.one_liner: Test object binding and permanence under occlusion in video foundation models by deleting early object tokens from predictor context.
2KvSYrWwH6.problem: Linear feature probes cannot tell whether video foundation models causally use object-centric structure in their predictions or maintain hidden objects under occlusion.
2KvSYrWwH6.method: The authors delete an object's early tokens from a frozen video predictor's context to measure per-object future prediction degradation via a parameter-free leakage ratio L, and measure object maintenance under occlusion via a fill contrast (POperm) and erased-history counterfactuals.
2KvSYrWwH6.key_idea: Measure causal object binding and occlusion permanence directly in a video model's predictions by deleting early object tokens and comparing prediction degradation and hidden-vs-occluder contrast.
2KvSYrWwH6.evidence: Evaluated across five video foundation models spanning three training paradigms, including V-JEPA2 (including V-JEPA2-H) and CogVideoX, on synthetic pilot scenes and real video controls.
2KvSYrWwH6.claimed_gains: Object binding leakage ratio reaches L = 0.23–0.43 in V-JEPA2 versus 1.00 untrained and 1.16 label-shuffled, while hidden-minus-occluder occlusion contrast POperm is never significantly positive across five models.
2KvSYrWwH6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that testing a video model's own prediction machinery via token-deletion and erased-history counterfactuals is a well-motivated diagnostic for distinguishing feature decodability from causal object use.
2KvSYrWwH6.main_concern: A predictive model trained on visible pixels is expected to predict the visible occluder at an occluded location, so a non-positive output-space contrast (POperm) does not rule out persistent object maintenance in internal states.

wBmaKUqoBB.one_liner: Decompose federated black-box VLM adaptation into zeroth-order mean-contrast prompt search and closed-form global score-space residual refinement.
wBmaKUqoBB.problem: Federated prompt adaptation of vision-language models typically requires white-box gradient or feature access, whereas black-box API interfaces only accept prompts and return class scores.
wBmaKUqoBB.method: FedMUSE parameterizes textual and visual prompts with common and differential latent kernels for block-wise zeroth-order search, then freezes the prompt predictor and solves a global residual refinement in the shared class-score space using pooled additive client statistics.
wBmaKUqoBB.key_idea: Separate zeroth-order query search for continuous multimodal prompts from an analytical global residual fit computed over pooled client statistics in the output score space.
wBmaKUqoBB.evidence: Evaluated across 13 datasets and multiple client partitions over three random seeds.
wBmaKUqoBB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating zeroth-order prompt search from analytical pooled score-space refinement is a well-reasoned design supported by thorough experiments across 13 datasets.
wBmaKUqoBB.main_concern: Global residual refinement on zero-shot CLIP alone accounts for nearly all the accuracy gain—with a 69.16% vs. 65.16% text-table discrepancy leaving the expensive prompt search's value unclear—and requires dense class-score vectors and balanced client coverage.

HlVU2N2sHx.one_liner: Extract executable Blender Python reconstructions and reusable procedural knowledge from tutorial videos to augment 3D coding agents.
HlVU2N2sHx.problem: Large language models struggle to generate 3D assets with complex geometry, rigging, and simulation because expert intermediate workflows in tutorial videos are difficult to extract and reuse.
HlVU2N2sHx.method: BlenderLore converts internet tutorial videos into illustrated workflows, reconstructs assets in executable Blender Python, and combines methods across tutorials to build a procedural knowledge library packaged as BlenderLore Skill alongside a 100-task benchmark (BlenderLore-Bench).
HlVU2N2sHx.key_idea: Reconstruct tutorial videos into executable Blender Python workflows and cross-tutorial combinations to build a reusable procedural skill library for 3D coding agents.
HlVU2N2sHx.evidence: Constructed ~22K project instances from over 3K videos and evaluated leading LLMs on BlenderLore-Bench covering 100 tasks across eight Blender capabilities.
HlVU2N2sHx.claimed_gains: Expands the collection to about 22K project instances associated with over 3K videos and introduces a 100-task benchmark covering eight Blender capabilities.
HlVU2N2sHx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extracting intermediate procedural workflows from tutorial videos and evaluating functional 3D scene structure addresses an important data gap for 3D coding agents.
HlVU2N2sHx.main_concern: Experiments only compare unaugmented agents against the full BlenderLore Skill package without isolating individual components or comparing against simpler baselines like raw transcripts, documentation, or code retrieval.

899Uym6doj.one_liner: Assign turn-level content and temporal counterfactual credit to omni-modal perception actions and selectively distill beneficial teacher interventions.
899Uym6doj.problem: Outcome-only reinforcement learning in omni-modal active perception obscures which specific turn, modality, and temporal interval contributed useful evidence versus redundant or misleading acquisitions.
899Uym6doj.method: Modality-Attributed Turn-Level Credit Assignment (MATCA) uses explicit media counterfactuals to compute signed content and temporal-specificity credits routed to responsible action-value fields, while Selective Intervention Consolidation (SIC) distills teacher actions only when student-completed branches outperform the student's own rollouts.
899Uym6doj.key_idea: Evaluate media counterfactuals at each perception turn to route signed content and temporal-specificity credits to specific action fields, decoupling evidence acquisition quality from final trajectory success.
899Uym6doj.evidence: Evaluated on omni-modal benchmarks including Daily-Omni, OmniVideoBench, JointAVBench, Video-MME, and LVOmniBench with ablations on credit components and selective distillation.
899Uym6doj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling turn-level evidence acquisition quality from trajectory-level outcome rewards addresses a clear credit-assignment bottleneck in active perception, supported by clean component ablations.
899Uym6doj.main_concern: The real-versus-null counterfactual credits the chosen modality type without comparing alternative modalities on the same interval, and evaluations lack variance estimates and direct proof that trained policies reduce unhelpful acquisitions.

xIxco3foES.one_liner: Stabilize single-policy on-policy self-distillation by storing sparse historical next-token distributions as fixed function-space targets.
xIxco3foES.problem: In on-policy self-distillation for language model reasoning, the feedback-informed self-teacher evolves alongside the student, creating unstable moving targets or requiring memory-heavy teacher weight copies.
xIxco3foES.method: Function-Space Temporal Self-Distillation (FTSD) stores sparse historical next-token distributions in a quality- and coverage-aware temporal memory as fixed distillation targets, combined with privileged disagreement correction and reliability-adaptive reference grounding.
xIxco3foES.key_idea: Store sparse historical next-token probability distributions in function space as fixed temporal targets to stabilize self-distillation without maintaining a separate parameter-space teacher model.
xIxco3foES.evidence: Evaluated across reasoning and tool-use benchmarks on two LLM backbones including Olmo3-7B-Instruct under a 5-hour training budget.
xIxco3foES.claimed_gains: Outperforms the strongest baseline by approximately 4 percentage points on average under a 5-hour training budget while reducing peak memory usage from about 70 GB to 56 GB on Olmo3-7B-Instruct.
xIxco3foES.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that caching sparse historical output distributions in function space is a practical way to mitigate teacher drift and reduce GPU memory overhead while improving accuracy.
xIxco3foES.main_concern: The conceptual distinction from prior function-space logit replay (such as Dark Experience Replay) is under-explained, and ablations do not isolate temporal consolidation from the added ground-truth cross-entropy reference grounding.

ECTECsupU8.one_liner: Decouple visual feature specialization from text-guided semantic conditioning and distill teacher knowledge across Euclidean and hyperbolic spaces.
ECTECsupU8.problem: Injecting semantic priors directly into shared multimodal features and distilling teacher knowledge solely via Euclidean matching interferes with low-level visual details in infrared-visible image fusion.
ECTECsupU8.method: PSDFusion constructs local-detail and context-preserving features via asymmetric transformations and cross-gating before applying text-guided semantic conditioning, and combines Euclidean and hyperbolic-aware student refinements aligned with multi-level teacher features in a channel-correlation space.
ECTECsupU8.key_idea: Separate low-level visual specialization from text-guided conditioning and align combined Euclidean and Poincaré-ball tangent-space student features with teacher channel correlations.
ECTECsupU8.evidence: Evaluated on four infrared-visible image fusion benchmarks (including MSRS, LLVIP, FMB, M3FD) and two downstream perception tasks (semantic segmentation and object detection) against 12 baselines.
ECTECsupU8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating low-level visual feature specialization from semantic text conditioning is a well-motivated design evaluated across four fusion benchmarks and two downstream tasks.
ECTECsupU8.main_concern: The hyperbolic pathway maps features to the Poincaré ball and back to Euclidean space without using geodesic distances or hyperbolic objectives, leaving its geometric advantage over a nonlinear Euclidean transformation unsubstantiated.

80vI5guhxw.one_liner: Explain diffusion model generalization-before-memorization via a two-bulk spectral split in the NTK Gram matrix caused by repeated noising.
80vI5guhxw.problem: Diffusion models trained on finite datasets first generalize to novel samples and only much later memorize training data, but the exact dynamical mechanism separating these timescales is unclear.
80vI5guhxw.method: The authors analyze score-matching training dynamics in the lazy regime via the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) Gram matrix evaluated on m noised copies per training sample, solving its spectrum analytically in high-dimensional linear and polynomial sample-complexity regimes.
80vI5guhxw.key_idea: Multiple noise realizations per training sample split the NTK Gram matrix spectrum into a large-eigenvalue bulk carrying global distribution features and a small-eigenvalue bulk aligned with sample-specific noise.
80vI5guhxw.evidence: Supported by analytical high-dimensional spectrum derivations in linear (n ~ d) and polynomial (n ~ d^k) regimes, convolutional NTK truncation experiments, and finite-width U-Net spectral measurements.
80vI5guhxw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that linking multiple noise realizations per sample to a two-bulk NTK Gram matrix spectrum and eigenvector structure provides a clear theoretical explanation for the timescale separation between generalization and memorization.
80vI5guhxw.main_concern: The theoretical analysis assumes a lazy training regime, a single fixed diffusion timestep, and a finite fixed set of noise realizations rather than online noise resampling and feature learning across timesteps.

D39sCVuJkb.one_liner: Accelerate convex optimization under (H0, H1)-smoothness using Nesterov acceleration with a two-regime weight schedule and realized curvature correction.
D39sCVuJkb.problem: Convex optimization under generalized (H0, H1)-smoothness—where the Hessian norm grows linearly with suboptimality—lacks accelerated full-gradient and randomized coordinate convergence guarantees.
D39sCVuJkb.method: The authors combine Nesterov acceleration with a two-regime weight schedule and realized curvature correction to derive accelerated full-gradient and uniform/non-uniform randomized coordinate methods, paired with matching lower bounds.
D39sCVuJkb.key_idea: Combine Nesterov acceleration with a two-regime weight schedule and realized curvature correction to decouple H0 and H1 dependencies in (H0, H1)-smooth convex optimization.
D39sCVuJkb.evidence: Supported by theoretical oracle complexity upper and lower bounds and empirical comparisons on two real-data generalized linear models.
D39sCVuJkb.claimed_gains: Achieves full-gradient oracle complexity O(R sqrt(H0 / epsilon) + R sqrt(H1) log(1 / epsilon)) with optimal H1 dependence up to logarithmic factors.
D39sCVuJkb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper provides the first accelerated full-gradient and coordinate-descent complexity guarantees that separate H0 and H1 for convex (H0, H1)-smooth optimization.
D39sCVuJkb.main_concern: The algorithm adapts existing AGMsDR techniques, requires knowing the optimal objective value f*, and lacks compelling practical examples of functions that are (H0, H1)-smooth but not covered by standard or (L0, L1)-smoothness.

qIry5Fukv7.one_liner: Augment DRL job-shop schedulers with analytical resource-capacity action descriptors and completion-loss certificate penalties.
qIry5Fukv7.problem: Deep reinforcement learning schedulers for flexible job-shop scheduling rely on learned state representations without explicitly reasoning about whether candidate assignments preserve sufficient resource capacity to avoid future bottlenecks.
qIry5Fukv7.method: Resource-Capacity Reasoning (RCR) is an encoder-agnostic framework that appends a four-feature Balanced-Capacity Descriptor (BCD) of residual capacity pressure to each candidate action representation and adds a Completion-Loss Certificate (CLC) auxiliary reward penalty based on a heuristic reference horizon.
qIry5Fukv7.key_idea: Augment candidate scheduling actions with analytical residual capacity-pressure descriptors and penalize policy updates using a horizon-based completion-loss certificate without altering the state encoder.
qIry5Fukv7.evidence: Evaluated across three GNN/Transformer scheduling backbones, PPO and REINFORCE algorithms, and synthetic and public benchmarks for FJSP, JSSP (Taillard, DMU), and FFSP.
qIry5Fukv7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that RCR is an encoder-agnostic, modular addition that consistently improves scheduling performance across multiple neural backbones and problem variants without requiring optimal labels.
qIry5Fukv7.main_concern: Computing capacity descriptors and reference horizons for every feasible action at every step introduces unquantified wall-clock overhead, and cumulative CLC penalties are not guaranteed to align with makespan minimization.

xBVd5mTJvz.one_liner: Smooth teacher communication Q-functions over latent cross-agent observation distributions to prevent negative transfer to decentralized MARL students.
xBVd5mTJvz.problem: Distilling communicating multi-agent policies into decentralized execution (CTDE) students causes policy discrepancy and negative transfer when the teacher relies on non-local information unavailable at test time.
xBVd5mTJvz.method: Communication Smoothing Distillation (CSD) models cross-agent conditional observation distributions in a latent space, uses gradient ascent to find communication variations that maximize teacher Q-value discrepancy, and applies a smoothing penalty before distilling Q-value targets into CTDE students.
xBVd5mTJvz.key_idea: Penalize teacher Q-value sensitivity to adversarial perturbations sampled from a learned conditional distribution of other agents' observations before distilling Q-values into decentralized policies.
xBVd5mTJvz.evidence: Supported by theoretical Q-smoothing representability conditions and empirical evaluations on predator-prey, restricted-visibility SMAC, and Google Research Football integrated with VDN, QMIX, and Qatten.
xBVd5mTJvz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reducing a communication teacher's sensitivity to non-local information addresses a real negative-transfer problem in CTDE distillation and yields strong results on partially observable SMAC tasks.
xBVd5mTJvz.main_concern: The adversarial search and variational distribution learning shows discrepancies between the mathematical formulation and the implementation—including a zero gradient at initialization for deterministic teachers—and latent perturbations may not cover true joint observation variations.

u1ABe44k44.one_liner: Perform test-time subgame solving in imperfect-information games via policy-gradient RL with an implicit state-sampler gadget.
u1ABe44k44.problem: Principled test-time policy improvement in two-player zero-sum imperfect-information games is restricted to tabular subgame construction or single gradient step updates.
u1ABe44k44.method: The authors extend tabular gadget games to reinforcement learning by training an implicit state sampler and a virtual actor policy instead of explicitly constructing the subgame, and use fixed-reference policy regularization to bound strategy changes during Bayesian subgame solving.
u1ABe44k44.key_idea: Replace explicit tabular gadget construction with a learned state sampler, virtual actor, and fixed-reference regularization to run multi-step policy-gradient subgame solving at test time.
u1ABe44k44.evidence: Supported by theoretical bounds on regularized strategy change and empirical evaluations measuring exploitability in small games and head-to-head play against blueprints and update-equivalence in larger games.
u1ABe44k44.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending subgame solving to policy-gradient reinforcement learning via an implicit gadget avoids explicit subgame construction and is clearly presented.
u1ABe44k44.main_concern: The theoretical guarantees do not fully match the implemented algorithm—with gaps in the sequence-form proof, trajectory vs. strategy regularization, and loss of standard resolving safety guarantees—and experimental benchmarks are relatively small.

7Oj3u2NoeY.one_liner: Preserve vision encoder patch relations and project them into frozen LLM decoders for compute-efficient VLM training.
7Oj3u2NoeY.problem: When integrating frozen vision encoders into pretrained language decoders, visual representation structure can degrade across the encoder readout, projector, and decoder layers.
7Oj3u2NoeY.method: The feiner framework diagnoses and preserves modality-specific visual representations across the encoder, MLP projector (using intermediate-layer readout, centroid bias, Gram loss, and register tokens), and language decoder in LLaVA-style vision-language models.
7Oj3u2NoeY.key_idea: Combine frozen intermediate vision-encoder readouts, structure-preserving projector regularization, and register tokens to maintain patch relationships and decoder-side visual information flow.
7Oj3u2NoeY.evidence: Evaluated on single-image understanding benchmarks using compact LLaVA-style models (including FEINER-450M) with SmolLM-family decoders alongside representation and attention analyses.
7Oj3u2NoeY.claimed_gains: Rivals state-of-the-art models at comparable scale while requiring less than half the compute.
7Oj3u2NoeY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper provides a well-structured stage-by-stage diagnostic of visual information preservation and an efficient frozen-encoder training recipe.
7Oj3u2NoeY.main_concern: The framework assembles existing components selected via an unvalidated internal metric, is tested only on SmolLM decoders for single-image tasks, and lacks direct comparisons to closely related representation-alignment methods like VIRAL.

XkA62IAa77.one_liner: Factorize driving scene features into Context, Map, and motion-aligned Evolution tokens for hierarchical end-to-end trajectory planning.
XkA62IAa77.problem: Existing end-to-end autonomous driving planners mix global context, local geometry, and temporal dynamics into a single unified representation without differentiating their distinct planning roles.
XkA62IAa77.method: RoleDrive decomposes shared visual features into Context Tokens for global scene context, Map Tokens for local spatial geometry, and Evolution Tokens computed as residuals between ego-motion-aligned historical and current Map representations, integrating them progressively for trajectory reasoning.
XkA62IAa77.key_idea: Separate driving scene features into global Context Tokens, local spatial Map Tokens, and motion-aligned temporal residual Evolution Tokens for coarse-to-fine trajectory planning.
XkA62IAa77.evidence: Evaluated on NAVSIM-v1, NAVSIM-v2, and the closed-loop photorealistic HUGSIM benchmark with a 36.9M-parameter model.
XkA62IAa77.claimed_gains: With 36.9M parameters and no extra training data, achieves 94.9 PDMS on NAVSIM-v1 (surpassing the human-driver baseline) and state-of-the-art results on NAVSIM-v2 and HUGSIM.
XkA62IAa77.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating global context, local BEV geometry, and ego-motion-aligned temporal residuals is a coherent, lightweight architecture with strong benchmark numbers on NAVSIM.
XkA62IAa77.main_concern: The design combines existing mechanisms (such as motion-aligned residuals and staged attention), and small single-seed ablation gains (0.2–0.5 PDMS) do not conclusively prove that explicit role separation outperforms a capacity-matched conventional fusion baseline.

HzKNgMa3rC.one_liner: Enforce contextual integrity in LLM persistent memory via a hypernetwork generating Stiefel frames for asymmetric attention beamforming.
HzKNgMa3rC.problem: LLMs with persistent memory use retained user information indiscriminately across contexts, causing privacy violations that external prompt filters or rigid retrieval controls fail to balance against obligatory memory use.
HzKNgMa3rC.method: MemSAGE uses a lightweight hypernetwork to dynamically generate orthonormal Stiefel frames for the current context and retained memories, forming a nested permission-demand geometry that applies asymmetric beamforming over LLM query-key attention to suppress inappropriate memories and amplify obligatory ones.
HzKNgMa3rC.key_idea: Generate context- and memory-specific Stiefel manifold frames via a hypernetwork to directionally suppress impermissible memories and amplify required ones in frozen LLM attention.
HzKNgMa3rC.evidence: Evaluated across four frozen LLM backbones and two datasets including CIMemories (tested on three held-out profiles and 147 contexts).
HzKNgMa3rC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling asymmetric permission and demand norms via geometric attention steering on a frozen LLM backbone is a modular and well-motivated alternative to hard retrieval filtering.
HzKNgMa3rC.main_concern: The empirical evaluation relies on a small single split (3 profiles, 147 contexts) without multi-seed variance or classifier metrics, and does not verify whether leakage reduction stems from permission suppression or why a Stiefel manifold is necessary over simpler subspace methods.

eV8wL3bQad.one_liner: Augment frozen terminal agents by retrieving positive execution Skills and contrastive failure Memories distilled from past trajectories.
eV8wL3bQad.problem: Terminal agents fail on long-horizon command tasks where minor errors alter environment state, while fine-tuning and RL require costly executable environments and large trajectory corpora.
eV8wL3bQad.method: STRATA distills past terminal trajectories into a stratified external library of Skills (capturing successful execution patterns) and Memories (extracting failure lessons by contrasting paired successful and failed attempts), using agentic retrieval to inject relevant entries into the prompt of a frozen backbone.
eV8wL3bQad.key_idea: Distill past terminal trajectories into hierarchical execution Skills and contrastive success-versus-failure Memories retrieved agentically into the prompt without updating model weights.
eV8wL3bQad.evidence: Evaluated on Terminal-Bench 1.0 and Terminal-Bench 2.0 across multiple LLM backbones including DeepSeek-V4-Pro and Qwen3-32B.
eV8wL3bQad.claimed_gains: On Terminal-Bench 2.0, STRATA achieves a mean pass rate of 63.3% across three runs with DeepSeek-V4-Pro.
eV8wL3bQad.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that STRATA delivers clear, well-controlled pass-rate improvements across multiple backbones under a shared trajectory pool and evaluation budget.
eV8wL3bQad.main_concern: The experiments do not compare paired success-failure contrastive extraction against extracting lessons from successful and failed trajectories independently while holding the agentic retriever and prompt budget fixed.

8Kb0ZLvCDi.one_liner: Audit whether task-affinity scores justify pairwise multi-task configuration choices across mechanism, preference, and out-of-sample selection links.
8Kb0ZLvCDi.problem: Multi-task learning studies assume that a task-affinity score correlated with multi-task gain can reliably select which sharing or transfer configuration to deploy.
8Kb0ZLvCDi.method: The authors decompose affinity-based configuration selection into three inferential links—score to intervention effect, preferred configuration, and out-of-sample selection gain—and test them across 1,914 ordered task pairs from 172 tasks using fixed configuration portfolios and learned selectors.
8Kb0ZLvCDi.key_idea: Decompose task-affinity validation into mechanism tracking, architecture-dependent configuration preference, and out-of-sample selection gain beyond a small fixed portfolio of configurations.
8Kb0ZLvCDi.evidence: Tested on 1,914 ordered task pairs from 172 tasks spanning CelebA, QM9, and 16 multi-output regression families across multiple backbones (including a small CNN and ResNet-18).
8Kb0ZLvCDi.claimed_gains: Replacing a small CNN with ResNet-18 reduces adapted-transfer selection from 30% to 7% while task relations remain nearly unchanged, and a fixed portfolio of 2–3 configurations reduces oracle headroom below replicate noise on CelebA and QM9.
8Kb0ZLvCDi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating mechanism correlation from actionable configuration selection is an insightful problem formulation backed by an extensive empirical audit across 1,914 task pairs.
8Kb0ZLvCDi.main_concern: The study is restricted mainly to pairwise task combinations and offers cautious negative takeaways rather than a practical, low-cost method for multi-task grouping or configuration selection.

ASE0YO1DzY.one_liner: Benchmark audio LLMs on paired same-or-different musical listening tests using answer-flipping musical edits and answer-preserving acoustic edits.
ASE0YO1DzY.problem: Standard audio LLM benchmarks evaluate high-level genre or mood descriptions rather than testing whether models can perceive basic differences in melody, harmony, timbre, and tempo without relying on answer bias.
ASE0YO1DzY.method: MusicListenBench pairs each listening item with a FLIP variant (changing melody, harmony, timbre, or tempo so the answer flips) and a STAY variant (adding acoustic perturbations like echo or hiss so the answer stays), evaluating 12 open and commercial audio LLMs alongside GRPO post-training.
ASE0YO1DzY.key_idea: Pair each same-or-different musical clip comparison with an answer-changing musical edit and an answer-preserving acoustic perturbation to cancel response bias and separate sensitivity from invariance.
ASE0YO1DzY.evidence: Evaluated 8 open audio LLMs, 4 commercial models (including GPT-Audio and Gemini 2.5 Pro), human listeners, and GRPO post-training on 10k rendered clean pairs (e.g., Qwen2.5-Omni) across symbolic rendered and real recording test sets.
ASE0YO1DzY.claimed_gains: Seven of eight open models score within 4 points of the 50% chance floor; Gemini 2.5 Pro reaches 74.2% versus 87.0% for humans; GRPO raises Qwen2.5-Omni from 61.2% to 99.0% on clean pairs and 86.0% on FLIP/STAY (missing 1.9% of changes vs. 24.7% for Gemini 2.5 Pro).
ASE0YO1DzY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark addresses an important perceptual gap in audio LLMs and that the paired FLIP/STAY design effectively cancels letter bias and reveals robustness failures.
ASE0YO1DzY.main_concern: The training and main test sets rely heavily on simplified synthetic single-instrument MIDI/SoundFont audio, and GRPO post-training was only run on clean pairs without acoustic augmentation baselines.

pUmxcBYyHZ.one_liner: Cache top-scoring tokens by delta-rule update magnitude in a small exact KV memory per Gated DeltaNet layer.
pUmxcBYyHZ.problem: Linear-attention and state-space models compress context into a fixed-size recurrent state that overwrites earlier associations, while hybrid recency KV caches discard distant tokens once they leave the local window.
pUmxcBYyHZ.method: HOLA (Hippocampal Linear Attention) augments each Gated DeltaNet layer with a small exact key-value memory that retains the top-scoring tokens ranked by the magnitude of the update each token commits to the recurrent state.
pUmxcBYyHZ.key_idea: Use the delta-rule recurrent update magnitude already computed at each step as an eviction score to retain poorly absorbed tokens in a small exact key-value cache.
pUmxcBYyHZ.evidence: Evaluated on 340M and 1B parameter models trained on 50B tokens across long-context retrieval (including 32k-token needle retrieval and RULER) and language modeling benchmarks against Gated DeltaNet and KDA.
pUmxcBYyHZ.claimed_gains: On a 32k-token sequence, HOLA's 64-slot memory holds the needle 29k tokens later while a same-size recency cache drops it, and at 1B parameters trained on 50B tokens it surpasses published Gated DeltaNet and KDA.
pUmxcBYyHZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing the zero-cost delta-rule update magnitude to select tokens for an exact KV cache is an intuitive, well-motivated mechanism demonstrated clearly at the 340M scale.
pUmxcBYyHZ.main_concern: The 1B model comparison relies on published baseline numbers without a matched author-trained 1B Gated DeltaNet control, while static write-time scores bias toward early tokens and add ~35% decoding latency.

mKWlMCJzhd.one_liner: Match protein pockets across geometry and chemistry using a joint spatial graph and separate multi-vector node representations.
mKWlMCJzhd.problem: Existing protein pocket matching methods compress geometric and chemical features into a single coarse vector and rely on ligand-similarity labels that obscure local geometric or chemical differences.
mKWlMCJzhd.method: GCMatch extracts cavity geometric points and chemical functional points into a unified neighborhood relation graph, encodes separate fine-grained node representations for geometry and chemistry with a graph encoder, and applies separate multi-vector matching to each set.
mKWlMCJzhd.key_idea: Connect cavity geometric points and chemical functional points in a joint spatial graph to learn separate node-level representations for multi-vector geometric and chemical pocket matching.
mKWlMCJzhd.evidence: Evaluated using a GVP-GNN encoder on a newly constructed four-quadrant dual-similarity benchmark with homology-based splits against baselines including OneProt.
mKWlMCJzhd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating geometric and chemical similarity via fine-grained multi-vector matching and evaluating on a four-quadrant hard-negative benchmark is well-motivated and achieves strong AUC.
mKWlMCJzhd.main_concern: Despite arguing that ligand similarity is a flawed proxy for pocket similarity, the benchmark still defines ground-truth chemical pocket similarity using bound-ligand ECFP4 Tanimoto similarity without validating downstream biological utility.

1fzQJPPIsk.one_liner: Isolate transferable privileged guidance in on-policy self-distillation by projecting hint-induced representation shifts onto a shared low-rank subspace.
1fzQJPPIsk.problem: In on-policy self-distillation, a self-teacher conditioned on full privileged solutions induces instance-specific representation shifts that the unprivileged student cannot reproduce at inference.
1fzQJPPIsk.method: PreSO conditions the self-teacher on compact hints rather than full solutions, estimates a leading low-rank subspace from privilege-induced representation shifts pooled across related problems, and projects the shift onto this subspace to construct a representation-level target for the student.
1fzQJPPIsk.key_idea: Condition the self-teacher on compact hints and project the resulting representation shift onto a cross-problem low-rank subspace before adding it to the student representation as a distillation target.
1fzQJPPIsk.evidence: Evaluated across three model scales (including Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-8B) and mathematical reasoning benchmarks with hint and positional ablations.
1fzQJPPIsk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that isolating recurring, transferable representation shifts from instance-specific privileged details is a clear motivation supported by consistent gains on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
1fzQJPPIsk.main_concern: Generalization beyond non-thinking mathematical reasoning is weak or unverified, and the method requires an external pipeline to generate privileged hints from ground-truth solutions.

j3AzgscTtz.one_liner: Unify discrete diffusion denoiser, bridge plug-in, and concrete score objectives as three coordinate parameterizations of the reversed CTMC.
j3AzgscTtz.problem: Discrete diffusion models are trained as denoisers, bridge plug-ins, or concrete scores under fragmented ELBO conventions, obscuring what probabilistic object each parameterization actually learns.
j3AzgscTtz.method: The authors derive the Oracle Distance identity linking negative ELBO to data entropy plus path KL divergence, and use a single Bregman projection argument under token-factorizing noise to derive exact conversions among denoiser, bridge plug-in (shown to learn the cavity distribution), and concrete score coordinates.
j3AzgscTtz.key_idea: Show via path-KL and Bregman projection that denoiser, cavity bridge plug-in, and concrete score objectives learn exact coordinate transformations of the same time-reversed continuous-time Markov chain.
j3AzgscTtz.evidence: Validated theoretically and empirically by training all three parameterizations with masked, uniform, and GIDD noise kernels on OpenWebText and uniform-diffusion solvers on four logic tasks.
j3AzgscTtz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper provides a clean, unifying mathematical perspective on discrete diffusion objectives—especially clarifying the bridge plug-in as the cavity distribution—supported by multi-kernel experiments.
j3AzgscTtz.main_concern: The theoretical results largely repackage established continuous-time Markov chain reversal, path-KL, Bregman projection, and cavity-distribution findings from recent literature with limited novel theoretical reach.

rseM9HVC7i.one_liner: Reshape gradient singular values in Muon optimization with a monotone sigmoid map approximated via Soft Newton-Schulz iterations.
rseM9HVC7i.problem: Matrix-valued optimizers like Muon use Newton-Schulz orthogonalization to nearly flatten the gradient singular spectrum, discarding relative magnitude information across gradient modes.
rseM9HVC7i.method: Soren (Spectral Orthogonal Reshaping) preserves gradient singular subspaces while applying a bounded, monotone sigmoid transformation to singular values—realized without SVD via a finite-depth Soft Newton-Schulz (SNS) polynomial iteration—to smoothly compress dominant modes without full flattening.
rseM9HVC7i.key_idea: Apply a finite-depth Soft Newton-Schulz polynomial iteration to impose a bounded sigmoid transformation on gradient singular values instead of fully flattening the spectrum.
rseM9HVC7i.evidence: Supported by convergence guarantees under relative smoothness and metric Polyak-Lojasiewicz geometry and empirical evaluations on C4 pre-training (four LLaMA sizes, Qwen3-0.6B), SFT (Qwen2.5-3B), and DPO (Mistral-7B).
rseM9HVC7i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly organized and demonstrates consistent empirical improvements over AdamW, Muon, and HTMuon across LLM pre-training, SFT, and DPO.
rseM9HVC7i.main_concern: The convergence theorems analyze an idealized full-gradient update rather than the implemented momentum/hybrid-AdamW algorithm, and do not prove a faster convergence rate than Muon or establish the finite-depth SNS approximation bound.

eLUJLZDg84.one_liner: InvisibleLoRA uses the shared base model to draft tokens and batches adapter verification once per speculative decoding cycle.
eLUJLZDg84.problem: Concurrent LoRA serving fragments adapter computation into small GPU-inefficient operations that repeat at every decoding token.
eLUJLZDg84.method: The shared base model drafts with LoRA disabled, and a LoRA-enabled pass verifies proposals for all served adapters while preserving target output distributions. A hybrid KV cache stores speculative base-model entries in the target model's cache.
eLUJLZDg84.key_idea: Share a LoRA-off drafter across adapters and amortize LoRA-on verification across speculative proposals.
eLUJLZDg84.evidence: Reviews describe tuned-baseline serving experiments, varied request-arrival patterns, acceptance-rate analyses, and alternative-drafter comparisons.
eLUJLZDg84.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find adapter-cost amortization a clear and practical solution that avoids a separate drafter's weights and cache.
eLUJLZDg84.main_concern: Acceptance-screened adapters and nonrepresentative task traffic leave the reported serving gains' generality unclear.

QKjbHYVJ1x.one_liner: Ray-Flow HMR samples 2D keypoints and depths along their camera rays before decoding body meshes with inverse kinematics.
QKjbHYVJ1x.problem: Probabilistic monocular mesh models struggle to jointly preserve accuracy, image consistency, and diversity in nonlinear body-parameter space.
QKjbHYVJ1x.method: An image-conditioned normalizing flow samples 2D keypoints, and a second conditional flow samples depths along their rays. A learned inverse-kinematics module converts the resulting 3D keypoints into meshes, with exact reprojection consistency at the intermediate keypoint stage.
QKjbHYVJ1x.key_idea: Factor uncertainty into image-plane keypoint locations and ray depths so sampled 3D joints reproject to their conditioning 2D points.
QKjbHYVJ1x.evidence: In-the-wild experiments include 3DPW and EMDB, probabilistic and deterministic comparisons, and a downstream view-selection study.
QKjbHYVJ1x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the ray-based factorization geometrically well motivated and its reprojection-consistency results promising.
QKjbHYVJ1x.main_concern: A matched unconstrained 3D-joint baseline is missing, so the benefit of ray-depth parameterization is not isolated.

2FrAxiYgNM.one_liner: CUA-Lite unifies computer-use environments, supervised data, and model harnesses for shared evaluation, reinforcement learning, and fine-tuning.
2FrAxiYgNM.problem: Fragmented computer-use resources prevent environments, datasets, and models from sharing scalable evaluation and training infrastructure.
2FrAxiYgNM.method: CUA-Lite standardizes an environment interface, supervised-data schema, and per-model harnesses that support evaluation, RL, and SFT. It integrates benchmarks, converts public datasets and fresh rollouts, and supplies lightweight VM-free desktop sandboxes.
2FrAxiYgNM.key_idea: Use shared environment, data, and model interfaces so the same harness executes agents and renders trajectories for training.
2FrAxiYgNM.evidence: The platform integrates 12 benchmarks, provides over 30,000 verifiable tasks and harnesses for 14 model families, and reports reference evaluation plus RL and SFT experiments.
2FrAxiYgNM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unified infrastructure and lightweight desktop sandboxes offer practical reuse for computer-use research.
2FrAxiYgNM.main_concern: Experiments do not sufficiently establish benefits attributable to the unified abstractions beyond conventional platform integration.

TYzMEzkbas.one_liner: RAPO anchors rewrite advantages to original-source rewards while combining competitive visibility and faithfulness objectives.
TYzMEzkbas.problem: Generative engine optimization often increases source visibility without adequately preserving the original content's faithfulness.
TYzMEzkbas.method: RAPO trains a rewriting policy using the original source reward as the advantage baseline and retains within-group standard-deviation normalization. Its composite reward combines faithfulness with visibility relative to the strongest competitor.
TYzMEzkbas.key_idea: Subtract the original source's reward from rewrite rewards and normalize within the candidate group while optimizing visibility and faithfulness.
TYzMEzkbas.evidence: Experiments span GEO-Bench, Researchy-GEO, and E-commerce, with model-size ablations, comparisons to RL methods, and transfer across generative engines.
TYzMEzkbas.claimed_gains: RAPO improves Overall visibility over the source by 9.34, 15.82, and 7.15 points on GEO-Bench, Researchy-GEO, and E-commerce, respectively, with better faithfulness.
TYzMEzkbas.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value including faithfulness in GEO optimization and the broad evaluation across benchmarks and engines.
TYzMEzkbas.main_concern: Reviewers find the source-baseline change technically limited and its gains modest under controlled comparisons.

vMVVyPYZk9.one_liner: ReDiffMark embeds sparse text watermarks through entropy-gated local re-diffusion and detects them by replaying the diffusion model.
vMVVyPYZk9.problem: Post-hoc text watermarking must balance small edits, stable detection signals, and computational cost.
vMVVyPYZk9.method: ReDiffMark edits high-entropy locations with key-seeded exponential-minimum sampling in a discrete diffusion language model. A replay-based, surprisal-weighted detector reruns the model on received text under a calibrated null hypothesis.
vMVVyPYZk9.key_idea: Locally re-diffuse entropy-selected tokens using keyed sampling, then detect their signal through model replay and surprisal weighting.
vMVVyPYZk9.evidence: Experiments span diffusion-model families, text sources, and passage lengths, with detector ablations, null calibration, and attack evaluations.
vMVVyPYZk9.claimed_gains: The abstract reports high single-passage detection at low edit rates with a constant two-forward-pass cost.
vMVVyPYZk9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value sparse editing, controlled detector ablations, and explicit reporting of failure cases.
vMVVyPYZk9.main_concern: Reviewers question detection reliability when key reuse or context-dependent randomness changes the assumptions behind null calibration.

FFXWYNO9QF.one_liner: Lexical Lens balances input-output lexical geometry and fits terminal-state predictors to read intermediate language-model states.
FFXWYNO9QF.problem: Native residual coordinates lack a shared lexical reference, making geometric interpretation sensitive to analysis coordinates and metric choices.
FFXWYNO9QF.method: Lexical Lens constructs a model-wide reference from the matrix geometric mean of input and output interface metrics. It predicts supported terminal-state components without decoder evaluation during fitting and applies information projection for lexical readout.
FFXWYNO9QF.key_idea: Balance reciprocal lexical interface metrics into a common geometry and fit intermediate-to-terminal state predictions in that reference.
FFXWYNO9QF.evidence: Mathematical analysis of geometry and calibration accompanies experiments across multiple model families and sizes against baselines including Tuned Lens.
FFXWYNO9QF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the motivated geometric formulation and empirical improvements in approximating final output distributions.
FFXWYNO9QF.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the implemented normalization, regularization, and gradient lifting preserve the claimed covariance of the complete estimator.

OixjU6ywHi.one_liner: HodgeDepth aligns local molecular-change directions and integrates them into a globally ordered tissue-depth coordinate.
OixjU6ywHi.problem: Spatial representation learning needs to connect local molecular variation with global tissue geometry.
OixjU6ywHi.method: HodgeDepth aligns noisy local directions and integrates them into a coherent depth coordinate across curved layers. It also constructs coordinates for recurrent layers and analyzes ordering, geometric bias, and canonical depth recovery.
OixjU6ywHi.key_idea: Orient local molecular-change directions consistently and integrate them into a global depth coordinate with a cumulative-spatial-mass scale.
OixjU6ywHi.evidence: Theory and synthetic examples accompany evaluations on 23 human cortical Visium sections across two cohorts, including the 12-section DLPFC benchmark.
OixjU6ywHi.claimed_gains: Mean absolute depth-layer Spearman correlation rises from 0.690 to 0.885, while mean clustering ARI reaches 0.618 versus 0.533 for SEDR, a 16% relative improvement.
OixjU6ywHi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the geometric formulation, theoretical analysis, and convincing depth-ordering results.
OixjU6ywHi.main_concern: Reviewers agree that differing downstream pipelines and incomplete controlled ablations prevent attributing clustering gains specifically to the depth representation.

dYMyhwbm46.one_liner: UMVR segments videos into adaptive events, combines local-global relevance, and allocates visual tokens by event informativeness.
dYMyhwbm46.problem: Predefined representation granularity separates short- and long-video retrieval, while long-video MLLM encoding incurs substantial token cost.
dYMyhwbm46.method: Length-Adaptive Event Representation divides each video into temporally coherent events with content-dependent extent. UMVR shares its backbone and scoring across video lengths, while Event-Aware Token Reduction compresses redundant events more aggressively.
dYMyhwbm46.key_idea: Use content-adaptive events for shared local-global retrieval scoring and allocate visual tokens according to event informativeness.
dYMyhwbm46.evidence: Experiments compare retrieval across seven benchmarks, including matched-backbone ActivityNet training and ablations of local and global information.
dYMyhwbm46.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the value of unified local-global retrieval and its favorable accuracy and encoding-cost trade-off.
dYMyhwbm46.main_concern: The efficiency evaluation leaves uncertainty about total token-budget matching and preprocessing costs for much longer videos.

BxU6L1tdoD.one_liner: CompWorld projects heterogeneous action streams into pretrained text space so separately trained controls can compose during video generation.
BxU6L1tdoD.problem: Action-specific video world models cannot reliably combine heterogeneous controls without paired multi-action training supervision.
BxU6L1tdoD.method: CompWorld retains precise action inputs while mapping type-specific encodings into a text-aligned action space. Learned missing-action placeholders and Action-to-Text Fusion condition the generator through Fused-Text Cross-Attention.
BxU6L1tdoD.key_idea: Map separate action streams into a shared pretrained text-conditioning interface with learned placeholders for absent action types.
BxU6L1tdoD.evidence: Compositional benchmarks combine keyboard with camera pose and robot-arm with camera pose only at inference, alongside separate-control evaluations.
BxU6L1tdoD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value composing heterogeneous controls without joint training annotations and the use of a pretrained text interface.
BxU6L1tdoD.main_concern: Reviewers question whether arm-plus-camera evaluations establish adherence to robot commands independently of camera following and plausible task-conditioned motion.

eyl7IAidAs.one_liner: OptEvolve searches typed optimization genomes, rejects invalid iterations symbolically, and tunes solver kernels for target hardware.
eyl7IAidAs.problem: Choosing formulations, algorithms, and hardware implementations is difficult, while unconstrained code mutation lacks mathematical convergence guarantees.
eyl7IAidAs.method: OptEvolve co-optimizes formulations, algorithmic schemes, and operator implementations using typed genomes in a monotone-operator calculus. A symbolic gate filters invalid candidates, while behavioral contracts and an empirical cost model guide kernel and GPU fusion tuning.
eyl7IAidAs.key_idea: Search a typed monotone-operator grammar under symbolic convergence checks, then tune admitted implementations against hardware cost.
eyl7IAidAs.evidence: Experiments compare specialist and general-purpose solvers on structured problems and held-out QP, LP, and SOCP benchmarks.
eyl7IAidAs.claimed_gains: Targeted CUDA fusion tiles outperform XLA by up to 2.7×.
eyl7IAidAs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value incorporating correctness conditions into solver search and jointly considering mathematical and hardware choices.
eyl7IAidAs.main_concern: Reviewers question how much LLM-guided discovery adds beyond configuring established solver components or simpler search and routing.

QnK7LqSbgR.one_liner: Sparse 2D surfels bake neural spatial texture into a hardware-accelerated atlas, removing runtime network evaluation.
QnK7LqSbgR.problem: Per-frame neural appearance evaluation makes high-quality splatting costly for real-time and resource-constrained rendering.
QnK7LqSbgR.method: The method separates low-frequency geometry and view-dependent surfel appearance from view-independent high-frequency texture learned through a spatial hash grid. Adaptive atlas baking and a falloff sparsity objective yield compact textured primitives for rendering.
QnK7LqSbgR.key_idea: Distill view-independent hash-grid appearance into a texture atlas while retaining sparse surfel geometry and view-dependent color.
QnK7LqSbgR.evidence: Multiple rendering benchmarks compare quality and speed with splatting baselines and ablate kernels, sparsity regularization, atlas baking, and fine-tuning.
QnK7LqSbgR.claimed_gains: The method renders roughly 7 to 9× faster than 3DGS on common benchmarks and over an order of magnitude faster on individual scenes.
QnK7LqSbgR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize substantial rendering-efficiency gains with competitive perceptual quality and detailed implementation evidence.
QnK7LqSbgR.main_concern: Reviewers find the contribution difficult to isolate from existing surfel components and unmatched baking or rendering optimizations in close baselines.

604Rvafrkn.one_liner: Optimal-transport feature fusion and spatial-functional text adaptation jointly ground semantic parts and affordances over reconstructed complete 3D objects.
