604Rvafrkn.problem: Robots need semantic and affordance information about occluded regions, but existing approaches handle visible regions or separate the two tasks.
604Rvafrkn.method: The framework reconstructs a complete object from one image and aligns image and shape features through optimal transport with spatial and cross-instance consistency. It adds spatial-functional cues to text embeddings and provides multilevel semantic and affordance annotations.
604Rvafrkn.key_idea: Fuse image and shape features with optimal transport and adapt text embeddings to link object parts with their functions.
604Rvafrkn.evidence: Simulation and real-world evaluations include PartNet and 3DAffordanceNet comparisons with 2D and 3D baselines under occlusion.
604Rvafrkn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value joint full-object semantic and affordance grounding from partial observations and report strong empirical results.
604Rvafrkn.main_concern: Reviewers question whether restricted query templates and training-time text augmentation support the claimed query generalization.

9euH4aDEsO.one_liner: A preconditioned stochastic past extragradient method uses independent normalization samples to solve variational inequalities beyond standard Lipschitz assumptions.
9euH4aDEsO.problem: Most stochastic variational-inequality methods require global or generalized Lipschitz continuity that excludes broader operator classes.
9euH4aDEsO.method: The method applies stochastic past extragradient updates under relaxed regularity and bounded oracle variance. Independent samples for update direction and nonlinear normalization address preconditioning bias.
9euH4aDEsO.key_idea: Separate stochastic direction and normalization samples in a preconditioned past extragradient update under relaxed operator regularity.
9euH4aDEsO.evidence: Analysis establishes almost-sure convergence and fixed-horizon guarantees in expectation and probability, alongside numerical comparisons with standard extragradient methods.
9euH4aDEsO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the motivation for broader operator assumptions and the value of stochastic convergence guarantees.
9euH4aDEsO.main_concern: Reviewers find the empirical comparisons insufficiently connected to the theory, with unmatched preconditioning and unverified assumptions or parameter conditions.

BzwvcBDrtY.one_liner: Controlled multilingual pretraining varies data quantity and difficulty coverage to measure how each shapes cross-lingual reinforcement-learning transfer.
BzwvcBDrtY.problem: The role of target-language pretraining exposure in determining reasoning gains transferred from another language's RL remains unclear.
BzwvcBDrtY.method: The study varies Korean pretraining quantity and arithmetic difficulty coverage before English, Korean, or bilingual RL. It tests mid-training on unseen difficulties and extends coverage and language comparisons to German, French, and Russian.
BzwvcBDrtY.key_idea: Hold source-language training fixed while varying target-language data quantity and difficulty coverage before applying language-specific RL.
BzwvcBDrtY.evidence: Controlled synthetic arithmetic experiments examine English-Korean transfer, with abstract-reported extensions to German, French, and Russian.
BzwvcBDrtY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled design and the finding that difficulty coverage matters more than additional data within an existing range.
BzwvcBDrtY.main_concern: Reviewers question generalization from small models and synthetic arithmetic to larger multilingual models and diverse real-world language tasks.

vmi8aW0A5S.one_liner: TIDE completes short-speech topology, conditions continuous identity dynamics on it, and aggregates directional evidence for speaker verification.
vmi8aW0A5S.problem: Short utterances provide incomplete phonetic and temporal identity evidence that fixed-dimensional pooled embeddings do not explicitly model.
vmi8aW0A5S.method: TIDE builds position-velocity state clouds and persistent-homology descriptors, using a momentum long-view target to learn duration-gated topology completion. Completed topology modulates a neural controlled differential equation whose states form a time-weighted von Mises Fisher identity posterior.
vmi8aW0A5S.key_idea: Complete persistent topology from short acoustic observations, use it to condition identity dynamics, and aggregate states as directional evidence.
vmi8aW0A5S.evidence: Short-utterance verification experiments and ablations compare topology inside versus outside the CDE and include a parameter-matched MLP control.
vmi8aW0A5S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a coherent approach to incomplete speaker evidence and a useful coupling of topology with continuous dynamics.
vmi8aW0A5S.main_concern: Reviewers question baseline comparability because model identities, acoustic front ends, and enrollment or test protocols are not consistently matched.

nTpJPseDfl.one_liner: RaV renders candidate-specific views and uses a frozen vision-language model to verify and rerank 3D grounding hypotheses.
nTpJPseDfl.problem: Frozen 3D grounders often confuse same-class objects when appearance and confidence cannot resolve viewpoint-dependent relational cues.
nTpJPseDfl.method: RaV generates diverse candidates through transformed views and selects visibility-constrained candidate viewpoints with surrounding context. A frozen diffusion corrector cleans renderings before a frozen VLM verifies and reranks the hypotheses.
nTpJPseDfl.key_idea: Generate diverse grounding hypotheses, render candidate-conditioned viewpoints, and rerank candidates using frozen visual-language verification.
nTpJPseDfl.evidence: Experiments cover three grounders, multiple VLM families and scales, and three benchmarks, with consistent improvements across evaluated ScanRefer configurations.
nTpJPseDfl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a practical training-free plug-in that combines geometric localization with candidate-specific visual verification.
nTpJPseDfl.main_concern: Reviewers find the methodological contribution modest relative to existing candidate-verification grounding pipelines and request clearer comparisons.

3rtqQwxLHQ.one_liner: Fast-TD-MPC routes states between a distilled reactive policy and expensive model-predictive planning using a distance-based gate.
3rtqQwxLHQ.problem: Sampling and evaluating many trajectories at every step makes learned MPC too slow for demanding control frequencies.
3rtqQwxLHQ.method: Fast-TD-MPC keeps the pretrained world model and planner while adding fast policy execution and adaptive routing. A distance-based out-of-distribution gate reserves planning for states judged to need more deliberation.
3rtqQwxLHQ.key_idea: Distill planner behavior into a reactive policy and use a state-distance gate to choose between policy execution and planning.
3rtqQwxLHQ.evidence: Simulation experiments cover 103 continuous-control tasks, fixed-scheduling comparisons, ablations, and external-disturbance evaluations on DMControl.
3rtqQwxLHQ.claimed_gains: Fast-TD-MPC achieves up to approximately 4× faster inference and retains 95% of the planner's DMControl return under disturbances at half the mean step latency.
3rtqQwxLHQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simple selective-planning design and extensive simulation evaluation.
3rtqQwxLHQ.main_concern: Reviewers find the distinction from existing adaptive replanning methods unclear and the closest baseline comparisons incomplete.

wT2k544flc.one_liner: SKILLLITE extracts security evidence and intended functionality before compact language models adjudicate malicious behavior in agent skill packages.
wT2k544flc.problem: Compact local language models struggle to identify implicit malicious behavior in complex third-party agent skills.
wT2k544flc.method: SKILLLITE uses deterministic analyzers to extract security-relevant package behaviors and infers the skill's intended functionality. It synthesizes grounded evidence for structured maliciousness judgments by a compact LLM without executing the skill.
wT2k544flc.key_idea: Separate static evidence extraction and intent inference from compact-model risk adjudication over the complete skill package.
wT2k544flc.evidence: Evaluations cover three benchmarks, including an in-the-wild benchmark, and compare existing scanners with same-backbone direct zero-shot auditing.
wT2k544flc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value practical local auditing with compact models and the substantial benchmark evaluation.
wT2k544flc.main_concern: Reviewers find the central deterministic extraction rules and evidence construction insufficiently specified for reproduction.

0JYeMhnONw.one_liner: MASRubric distills failed trajectories into reusable checks that audit, revise, or withhold intermediate multi-agent messages.
0JYeMhnONw.problem: Errors in intermediate agent messages propagate downstream, while expert or reference-answer rubrics are unavailable for unseen messages.
0JYeMhnONw.method: MASRubric mines failed trajectories offline into criteria describing misconceptions, applicability conditions, and diagnostic checks. At runtime, retrieved criteria score each message and determine broadcasting, feedback-driven revision, or withholding.
0JYeMhnONw.key_idea: Retrieve failure-derived checks for each intermediate message and use criterion satisfaction to control its propagation or revision.
0JYeMhnONw.evidence: Experiments evaluate fixed and dynamic multi-agent frameworks across thirteen math and code benchmarks, including rubric transfer between Qwen3 model sizes.
0JYeMhnONw.claimed_gains: MASRubric achieves average accuracy gains of 2.83 and 1.74 percentage points on math reasoning and code generation benchmarks, respectively.
0JYeMhnONw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value converting historical failures into reusable context-specific checks for intermediate messages.
0JYeMhnONw.main_concern: Reviewers question gain reliability without repeated-run uncertainty estimates, particularly given stochastic agents and sensitivity to benchmark aggregation.

C1J4qonboY.one_liner: A fine-tuned model emits evaluation-recognition markers only in final responses, supplying labels for testing hidden-awareness detectors.
C1J4qonboY.problem: Reasoning-trace scans miss unverbalized evaluation awareness, and detector studies lack instance-level labels for that awareness.
C1J4qonboY.method: Synthetic document fine-tuning, SFT, and DPO train Qwen3.5-27B to emit a designated response marker when it recognizes evaluation while suppressing awareness in reasoning. The marker labels interactions for evaluating interpretability methods.
C1J4qonboY.key_idea: Train evaluation recognition into a final-response marker while suppressing reasoning-trace disclosure, then use that marker to assess detectors.
C1J4qonboY.evidence: Experiments test marker responses to evaluation framing and question cues and benchmark interpretability methods including linear probes and the Jacobian Lens.
C1J4qonboY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a concrete testbed for unverbalized awareness and the careful investigation of experimental confounds.
C1J4qonboY.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the marker identifies evaluation awareness or merely learned test-question formats and prompt rules.

RBB7QhM9ZX.one_liner: SIP oversamples clean examples under diverse non-eliciting prompts while inoculating contaminated examples to separate desired and undesired traits.
RBB7QhM9ZX.problem: Uniform inoculation prompting can leak unwanted behavior under unrelated prompts and impair desired behavior when clean demonstrations are scarce.
RBB7QhM9ZX.method: Stratified inoculation prompting assigns diverse non-eliciting prompts to oversampled clean examples while inoculating the remaining training data. The paper also explores backdoor dilution and password-locked inoculation.
RBB7QhM9ZX.key_idea: Assign clean and contaminated examples different prompt distributions so desired behavior receives supervision outside contexts requesting the undesired trait.
RBB7QhM9ZX.evidence: Controlled trait and harmful-advice experiments include matched-oversampling IP controls, ablations, and matched-step clean-only training comparisons.
RBB7QhM9ZX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a simple prompt-and-sampling intervention with evidence of reduced unwanted behavior and useful controlled comparisons.
RBB7QhM9ZX.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical advantage over training on the scarce clean subset alone, given retention-leakage trade-offs and unclear data-selection costs.

jg3AtLk2kn.one_liner: AMIGA combines mined graph motifs with centered additive feature, structure, and interaction channels for interpretable graph predictions.
jg3AtLk2kn.problem: Existing graph additive networks mix feature and topology effects, miss structural distinctions, and can spread spurious node relevance.
jg3AtLk2kn.method: AMIGA encodes topology with mined motifs and decomposes node contributions into feature, structural, and interaction channels. A training-data baseline weights graphs equally and centers the channels to define a unique decomposition under stated assumptions.
jg3AtLk2kn.key_idea: Represent topology through motif counts and center separate additive feature, structure, and feature-structure interaction contributions.
jg3AtLk2kn.evidence: Ten graph classification and regression benchmarks accompany synthetic explanation-recovery experiments, channel ablations, and a conditional uniqueness result.
jg3AtLk2kn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value explicit feature-structure decomposition and motif-based structural modeling as an extension of graph additive networks.
jg3AtLk2kn.main_concern: Reviewers find explanation validation too limited to establish stable, usable attributions beyond simple synthetic cases.

5xWHncSFqY.one_liner: Best-of-Depth minimizes the best prediction loss across recurrent depths to train looped Transformers as depth-wise candidate generators.
5xWHncSFqY.problem: Supervising only the final recurrent depth may underuse a looped Transformer's capacity to discover solutions along its trajectory.
5xWHncSFqY.method: Best-of-Depth optimizes the minimum prediction loss across depths within a fixed budget without changing the architecture. This treats successive recurrent predictions as candidate solutions rather than requiring the last depth alone to match the target.
5xWHncSFqY.key_idea: Backpropagate the best prediction loss across recurrent depths so any depth can satisfy the training target.
5xWHncSFqY.evidence: N-Queens completion, graph coloring, and code-generation experiments compare maximum-depth training, including beyond-training-depth and fixed-step-budget analyses.
5xWHncSFqY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simple alternative training objective and its evidence for solution discovery across recurrent depths.
5xWHncSFqY.main_concern: Reviewers question how to select a correct depth's candidate at inference without an external verifier, limiting the practical interpretation of discovery gains.

ExUqT99BWk.one_liner: Proves unbounded-logit Concept Bottleneck Models lack compact abductive explanations and remedies this via bounded probabilistic concepts and group-lasso sparsity
ExUqT99BWk.problem: Standard Concept Bottleneck Models with unbounded concept logits require every nonzero-weight concept to guarantee formal abductive faithfulness, making faithful explanations non-compact when bottlenecks are large.
ExUqT99BWk.method: Using formal abductive explainability, the authors prove that linear-head CBMs with unbounded concept activations admit no proper-subset faithful explanations. To enable compact faithful explanations and formal extraction algorithms, they bound the bottleneck using binary or categorical probabilistic concept variables and prune unused concepts during training via column-wise group lasso.
ExUqT99BWk.key_idea: Replace unbounded CBM concept logits with bounded probabilistic discrete variables and apply column-wise group-lasso sparsification so formal abductive explanations require only a small subset of concepts.
ExUqT99BWk.evidence: Supported by formal impossibility propositions for unbounded-logit CBMs and empirical evaluations of explanation size and accuracy across standard and VLM-based CBM architectures.
ExUqT99BWk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly formalizes an overlooked tension between formal faithfulness and explanation compactness in Concept Bottleneck Models.
ExUqT99BWk.main_concern: Impossibility under unbounded linear features follows directly from abductive explanation definitions, and empirical compactness gains come mainly from standard group-lasso concept pruning or simple activation bounding rather than probabilistic modeling.

rCjDSFK41m.one_liner: Server-side federated backdoor defense comparing layer-wise normalized singular-value energy distributions across client updates to apply graded coordinate restrictions
rCjDSFK41m.problem: Adaptive federated backdoor attacks match benign client updates in norm and direction while non-IID data heterogeneity causes benign updates to diverge, defeating geometric filtering defenses.
rCjDSFK41m.method: TIMBRE computes the scale-invariant normalized spectral energy distribution of each client's weight update layer by layer on the server without reference data. Updates whose spectral distributions deviate persistently from same-round peers receive graded coordinate-level dampening on unsupported components rather than binary client exclusion, with restrictions relaxed when anomalies subside.
rCjDSFK41m.key_idea: Detect anomalous client updates via deviations in layer-wise normalized singular-value energy distributions across same-round peers and apply graded coordinate-level suppression to unsupported update directions.
rCjDSFK41m.evidence: Evaluated across multiple image classification datasets and architectures under non-IID splits against five backdoor attacks and eight server-side federated defense baselines.
rCjDSFK41m.claimed_gains: Keeps every attack success rate in the main setting below 1.4% with a clean-accuracy cost of at most 1.5 percentage points, outperforming the eight evaluated defenses overall.
rCjDSFK41m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find analyzing scale-invariant layer-wise spectral energy distributions on the server without clean reference data intuitive and effective on the tested image-classification attacks.
rCjDSFK41m.main_concern: Skewed non-IID benign clients can also produce concentrated low-rank update spectra, advantages over prior singular-value defenses like MARS are unisolated, and inspecting raw client updates precludes secure aggregation.

t3JCEFGI5N.one_liner: Multi-turn agentic RL method selectively branching shared-prefix trajectories to estimate causal decision relevance and policy-weighted step credit
t3JCEFGI5N.problem: Trajectory-level terminal rewards in multi-turn LLM agent RL misattribute credit across steps, suppressing useful early decisions on failed rollouts and reinforcing flawed actions on successful ones.
t3JCEFGI5N.method: Dynamic Causal Tree (DCT) selectively expands shared-prefix counterfactual branches along anchor trajectories to perform same-history action interventions under a bounded rollout budget. Pairwise branch contrasts estimate each decision's causal relevance while policy-weighted aggregation computes signed step-level advantages used to update the anchor trajectory.
t3JCEFGI5N.key_idea: Selectively branch multi-turn agent trajectories from shared history prefixes and combine pairwise branch contrasts for causal relevance with policy-weighted rollouts for signed step-level credit.
t3JCEFGI5N.evidence: Supported by a credit-error policy-update bound and multi-hop retrieval QA experiments across two LLM families and multiple scales against trajectory-level and Tree-GRPO baselines, plus intervention faithfulness audits.
t3JCEFGI5N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating causal decision relevance from signed policy-update credit via shared-prefix counterfactual branching is conceptually sound and improves multi-hop QA over trajectory-level RL.
t3JCEFGI5N.main_concern: Dense jargon-heavy exposition obscures that population signed credit reduces to standard Q-minus-V, adaptive small-budget branching lacks a cost-matched Monte Carlo advantage baseline, and experiments cover only replayable retrieval QA.

F3XeCIIfU7.one_liner: Training-free scientific retriever pooling references cited by a query's nearest text neighbors and ranking them by neighbor votes
F3XeCIIfU7.problem: Dense text embeddings retrieve topically similar papers while missing essential baselines, datasets, and methods that lie beyond cosine rank 1,000 and are unreachable by text rerankers.
F3XeCIIfU7.method: Neighbourhood citation retrieval finds a query's nearest neighbors by dense text similarity, adds the documents cited by those neighbors into the candidate pool, and ranks candidates by how many neighbors cite them. This training-free local citation vote operates on top of existing text encoders and citation graphs.
F3XeCIIfU7.key_idea: Expand text-similarity retrieval candidates with outgoing citations from the query's nearest text neighbors and rank candidates by their local neighbor-citation count.
F3XeCIIfU7.evidence: Evaluated on the MasterSet must-cite benchmark, an eight-domain 4M-paper corpus, a 170M-paper corpus, and US patents with degree-preserving rewiring, popularity, and temporal and co-author controls.
F3XeCIIfU7.claimed_gains: Top-100 text similarity misses 61% of papers a study's experiments build on (with 30.8% of cited papers beyond cosine rank 1,000 in the 4M-paper corpus), while the training-free neighbour vote cuts MasterSet misses from 61% to 43%.
F3XeCIIfU7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly quantifies dense-retrieval recall limits for cited works and shows that training-free neighbor-citation voting substantially improves Recall@100 over text and popularity baselines.
F3XeCIIfU7.main_concern: Candidate expansion via nearest-neighbor citations closely resembles classic bibliographic-coupling and co-citation retrieval, lacks latency and index-maintenance benchmarks, and tests dense encoders without trained late-interaction models.

oUOiFJTGdN.one_liner: Input-adaptive frequency band partitioning using hard Top-K boundary selection and content-dependent spectral pooling for band-split audio source separation
oUOiFJTGdN.problem: Band-split audio source separators rely on fixed manual frequency partitions across all mixtures, merging discriminative spectral details or wasting band tokens on uninformative frequency regions.
oUOiFJTGdN.method: Dynamic Band Splitting (DBS) predicts mixture-conditioned boundary scores across STFT frequency blocks, selects band edges via hard Top-K under a fixed band-token budget, and pools variable-width subbands into tokens for standard separator backbones. After separation, it expands and refines tokens back onto the full STFT grid to predict complex masks.
oUOiFJTGdN.key_idea: Select mixture-specific STFT frequency band boundaries via hard Top-K scoring and content-dependent pooling under a fixed band-token budget before mask reconstruction.
oUOiFJTGdN.evidence: Evaluated across multiple band-split backbones (including BSRNN, TIGER, and MelRoFormer) on DnR v2, MUSDB18-HQ, and EchoSet with matched uniform-boundary and component ablations.
oUOiFJTGdN.claimed_gains: Improves separation across DnR v2, MUSDB18-HQ, and EchoSet, with DBS-BSRNN raising average SI-SDR from 7.7 to 9.1 dB on DnR v2 compared with retrained static BSRNN.
oUOiFJTGdN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and shows that input-adaptive frequency partitioning under a fixed band-token budget consistently improves SI-SDR across multiple datasets and backbones.
oUOiFJTGdN.main_concern: DBS increases total compute (MACs and FLOPs) by 55–62% for modest 0.3–1.4 dB SI-SDR gains without wall-clock timing, and modifies pooling and reconstruction simultaneously with dynamic boundaries.

GaKi2aZXvs.one_liner: Mitigates off-topic capability degradation from learned compressed KV-cache Cartridges via off-document teacher distillation and query-relevance routing
GaKi2aZXvs.problem: Learned KV-cache compression methods such as Cartridges are distilled solely on document-specific queries, causing context contamination and degraded general knowledge and instruction following on unrelated queries.
GaKi2aZXvs.method: The authors benchmark off-context derailment of learned KV caches across general knowledge, instruction following, and context contamination tasks. Cartridges++ augments Cartridge distillation with off-document queries supervised by the base no-context LLM and adds a lightweight query-relevance router to bypass the compressed cache on unrelated prompts.
GaKi2aZXvs.key_idea: Preserve general LLM capabilities alongside compressed document KV caches by mixing no-context teacher distillation on off-document prompts during training and gating cache activation by query relevance.
GaKi2aZXvs.evidence: Evaluated across two LLM families, four document datasets, and multiple compression ratios against heuristic KV-eviction baselines on on-context QA and off-context benchmarks (TinyMMLU, MMLU-Pro, IFEval).
GaKi2aZXvs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly exposes and quantifies off-context interference in learned KV-cache Cartridges and shows that off-document replay and routing restore general capabilities.
GaKi2aZXvs.main_concern: Both fixes—replay mixing with off-distribution data and OOD router gating—are standard remedies for narrow-domain fine-tuning, and evaluations test only starkly on-document versus completely unrelated queries.

h0Do3bIIud.one_liner: Joint confidence sets separate missed candidate coverage from selector-information loss and gate regret.
h0Do3bIIud.problem: An LLM can generate a correct answer without selecting it, while gating cannot recover candidates missed by every available action.
h0Do3bIIud.method: The same-pool audit decomposes unconverted opportunity into missed capture, information loss, and gate regret. One joint confidence set tests both proposal improvement and whether missed opportunity exceeds the remaining gate budget.
h0Do3bIIud.key_idea: A joint same-pool confidence set separates candidate-coverage limits from information loss and errors made by a selector gate.
h0Do3bIIud.evidence: Analyses include nine LiveAoPS and FEVEROUS comparisons, 20,000 new MedMCQA groups, a 4,494-group reasoning study, and reserved-question repairs for Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-30B-A3B.
h0Do3bIIud.claimed_gains: MedMCQA improves answer accuracy by 1.005 percentage points over direct answering but loses .470 points to unchanged plurality, while DPP repairs improve final accuracy by 4.69 and 6.25 percentage points on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-30B-A3B.
h0Do3bIIud.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing missed capture, information loss, and gate regret turns null selection results into useful diagnoses.
h0Do3bIIud.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the paper difficult to follow because of dense formalization, delayed definitions, and insufficient experimental detail.

lSG4d4Z5kM.one_liner: Blind-solver-certified question generation and recording-specific cross-modal graphs support multimodal instructional answering.
lSG4d4Z5kM.problem: Instructional QA benchmarks rarely combine speech, slides, documents, temporal dependencies, multi-hop connections, and long-context reasoning.
lSG4d4Z5kM.method: MM-AdvQAGen certifies modality, context, and multi-hop requirements through falsifiable blind-solver tests, producing MMAv-InstructBench from M3AV and SlideSpeech. MM-Graph-RAG links transcript, slide, and document content in recording-specific graphs with self-derived retrieval settings.
lSG4d4Z5kM.key_idea: Blind-solver falsification certifies evidence requirements, while a recording-specific cross-modal graph retrieves linked speech, slide, and document evidence.
lSG4d4Z5kM.evidence: The benchmark contains 4,624 questions across four reasoning dimensions, and evaluation includes multiple answerers, twelve baselines, modality ablations, retrieval measurements, and evidence swaps.
lSG4d4Z5kM.claimed_gains: On MMAv-InstructBench, MM-Graph-RAG improves judge accuracy over the strongest baseline by up to 10.7 percentage points.
lSG4d4Z5kM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adversarial question certification and cross-modal graph retrieval address meaningful shortcut and evidence-integration problems.
lSG4d4Z5kM.main_concern: Reviewers most often find that the contributions of graph retrieval and question certification are insufficiently isolated from prior or agentic alternatives.

Rl0Ur3UcoU.one_liner: Reconstruction-gain allocation assigns variable residual-code depths to document patches for compressed late-interaction retrieval.
Rl0Ur3UcoU.problem: Visual-document indexes must be compressed before queries are known even though queries determine which patches matter for matching.
Rl0Ur3UcoU.method: PARQ retains every patch and distributes a fixed residual-quantization budget according to document-side reconstruction-error reduction without query supervision or encoder fine-tuning. Grouped lookup-table scoring supports variable-depth codes without dense embedding reconstruction.
Rl0Ur3UcoU.key_idea: Marginal reconstruction gains determine per-patch residual-code depth, while depth-grouped lookup tables enable direct variable-length scoring.
Rl0Ur3UcoU.evidence: Experiments on ViDoRe v1 and v2 with ColPali and ColQwen2 compare allocation strategies and measure nDCG@5 and query latency on a 1M-patch index.
Rl0Ur3UcoU.claimed_gains: At 64× compression PARQ retains 90.3% and 89.2% of uncompressed nDCG@5 for ColPali and ColQwen2, respectively, retains 97.9% for both at 26×, and achieves 6.09 ms versus 39.11 ms query latency.
Rl0Ur3UcoU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adaptive precision allocation improves tight-budget retrieval and that grouped lookup tables provide a practical variable-depth implementation.
Rl0Ur3UcoU.main_concern: The baseline and ablation evidence does not fully establish advantages over stronger fixed-depth or external compression controls.

s24pLoMCc2.one_liner: Tangent-projected Newton–Schulz updates and separate radial steps independently control matrix direction and norm.
s24pLoMCc2.problem: Additive Muon-style updates couple weight-norm and direction changes, reducing the angular effect of later steps through incidental norm growth.
s24pLoMCc2.method: RODE factorizes each matrix into a scalar norm and unit-norm direction with independent learning rates. It updates the norm radially and projects stored momentum and every Newton–Schulz iterate into the tangent space before a spherical directional step.
s24pLoMCc2.key_idea: Momentum and Newton–Schulz iterates are tangent-projected so directional updates remain spherical while a separate scalar step controls norm.
s24pLoMCc2.evidence: Language and vision comparisons against Muon and related optimizers extend to 1.5B pretraining and 9B fine-tuning, with learning-rate tuning and downstream evaluations.
s24pLoMCc2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the radial-directional decomposition has a clear geometric motivation and is evaluated broadly with documented hyperparameter tuning.
s24pLoMCc2.main_concern: Reviewers most often find comparisons with norm-control alternatives incomplete, leaving the advantage over tuned fixed-norm and weight-decay baselines unclear.

0OWqFfufxl.one_liner: Collection maps, event logs, and learned verification prepare and evolve agent-native environments.
0OWqFfufxl.problem: Fragmented, misleading, conflicting, and evolving environmental evidence degrades agents performing context-dependent tasks.
0OWqFfufxl.method: Env-Rethink uses a 27B post-trained model to build Collection Maps and Event Logs, identify noise through offline trajectory learning, and evolve environments with virtual event histories. These components organize context, verify evidence, and generate harder verifiable challenges.
0OWqFfufxl.key_idea: Environment preparation explicitly organizes cross-file evidence and validates conflicting versions before virtual event histories alter states and relationships.
0OWqFfufxl.evidence: Experiments cover 30 workspace tasks, nine downstream models, held-out file-partition tests, environment preparation, and evolved-environment difficulty.
0OWqFfufxl.claimed_gains: Env-Rethink improves mean rubric pass rate by 18.7 percentage points on 30 workspace tasks.
0OWqFfufxl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evidence organization and validity checking address important practical agent failures and produce positive downstream results.
0OWqFfufxl.main_concern: Human validation and controlled comparisons are insufficient to establish that evolved tasks and downstream gains are valid and attributable.

355c9fSzPy.one_liner: Plan-regret corrections and exact budgeted planning convert hallucination scores into parent-preserving audit actions.
355c9fSzPy.problem: Under fixed human-review budgets, shared response-opening costs make independently ranked hallucination scores insufficient for choosing audits.
355c9fSzPy.method: PLAIT learns generator-hidden-state corrections to a frozen parent detector using plan regret, then exactly selects response, claim, and span actions with shared costs. A configurable constraint preserves parent-plan value, and a separate verifier recomputes feasibility.
355c9fSzPy.key_idea: Hidden-state corrections optimized for plan regret feed an exact shared-cost planner constrained to preserve estimated parent-detector value.
355c9fSzPy.evidence: Evaluation spans four generators, parent replacement, source-disjoint transfer, fixed-time recall, and an independent 84-participant human crossover study.
355c9fSzPy.claimed_gains: Claim-level PLAIT improves fixed-time recall by 3.54 percentage points over validation-selected exact score fusion, and PLAIT-C increases correctly identified unsupported characters per minute by 8.38% over exact fusion and 6.31% over a DeCCaF adapter.
355c9fSzPy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that shared-cost constrained planning is well motivated and that automatic and blinded human evaluations provide meaningful evidence.
355c9fSzPy.main_concern: Comparisons do not fully isolate plan-regret training and omit the strong DeCCaF baseline from the human study.

gl90dFAVUy.one_liner: Token-level teacher–student distribution interpolation creates exact intermediate rollouts for controllable policy distillation.
gl90dFAVUy.problem: Teacher-generated distillation traces are high-quality but mismatched to students, while student rollouts are learnable but often erroneous.
gl90dFAVUy.method: Interpolated Policy Distillation linearly combines teacher and student next-token distributions with an explicit coefficient. A speculative-decoding rule samples this interpolated policy exactly while reducing sequential teacher queries and naturally interleaving teacher and student segments.
gl90dFAVUy.key_idea: A token-wise interpolation coefficient directly controls the rollout distribution between teacher and student, with speculative decoding preserving that distribution exactly.
gl90dFAVUy.evidence: Prototype experiments separate rollout-policy effects from supervision, and evaluations compare student settings and benchmarks, including weak and pruned students.
gl90dFAVUy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicitly defining and exactly sampling an intermediate rollout policy is principled and produces gains in challenging student settings.
gl90dFAVUy.main_concern: Reviewers most often find that the quality and learnability metrics do not convincingly measure the trade-off motivating the method.

wOi9YUi1Tg.one_liner: Teacher–student discrepancy histories select rollback points for teacher-guided reconstruction during on-policy agent distillation.
wOi9YUi1Tg.problem: Delayed teacher intervention in agentic on-policy distillation can inherit environment changes caused by an earlier student mistake.
wOi9YUi1Tg.method: Rewind-OPD uses historical teacher–student discrepancies to choose an earlier intervention point, restores that state, and reconstructs the trajectory under teacher guidance before returning control to the student.
wOi9YUi1Tg.key_idea: Discrepancy history localizes an earlier trajectory state for rollback and teacher-guided reconstruction instead of intervening only at the current state.
wOi9YUi1Tg.evidence: Experiments cover three teacher–student pairs, three agentic benchmarks, six baselines, multiple student sizes, specialized and general teachers, and student-only testing.
wOi9YUi1Tg.claimed_gains: A general 30B teacher improves success over standard OPD by 4.1 and 4.7 percentage points for 1.7B and 4B students while reducing output tokens by 16.0% and 8.0%, and a specialized-teacher 4B student reaches 52.3% versus 51.9% for the teachers.
wOi9YUi1Tg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that retrospective rollback addresses a clear failure mode and is supported by relevant OPD baselines, ablations, and multiple environments.
wOi9YUi1Tg.main_concern: Reviewers agree that rollback changes training-data volume and teacher supervision, confounding attribution without matched token and interaction budgets.

Iyf3G75YFJ.one_liner: Projects full-modality teacher logit corrections onto a modality-constrained student's Fisher tangent space for missing-modality brain tumor segmentation.
Iyf3G75YFJ.problem: In missing-modality brain tumor segmentation, native logit distillation can push the student toward teacher predictions that rely on modalities unavailable to the student.
Iyf3G75YFJ.method: Manifold-Constrained Distillation (MCD) estimates a student-accessible tangent space from input perturbations and projects the teacher's logit correction onto it under Fisher geometry, retaining only the realizable target component.
Iyf3G75YFJ.key_idea: Projects teacher logit residuals onto an estimated student-accessible tangent subspace under Fisher geometry to filter out unrecoverable modality information.
Iyf3G75YFJ.evidence: Evaluated on BraTS 2018 and BraTS 2024 across all 15 nonempty modality combinations.
Iyf3G75YFJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that missing-modality MRI segmentation is clinically important and that addressing teacher-student information asymmetry via lightweight logit distillation is well-motivated.
Iyf3G75YFJ.main_concern: Reviewers question whether input-perturbation tangents capture the parameter-Jacobian reachable space, note missing norm-matched controls and unverified unlearnability of discarded corrections, and find reporting inconsistencies.

XbQw70QBqD.one_liner: Proves a Query-Access Impossibility Theorem showing black-box sampling prevents generators from being both jailbreak-robust and detectably broad on unidentifiable languages.
XbQw70QBqD.problem: How black-box query access enables jailbreaking and limits the joint achievability of safety robustness and generation breadth from positive training data is not theoretically characterized.
XbQw70QBqD.method: The authors formalize query-access robustness and detectable breadth for generators trained on positive samples and prove that any robust, detectably broad generator yields a black-box membership estimator, implying impossibility for non-identifiable prefix-closed language classes.
XbQw70QBqD.key_idea: Reduces black-box membership estimation to sampling a robust and detectably broad generator on a fixed prompt batch.
XbQw70QBqD.evidence: Theoretical proofs (Query-Access Impossibility Theorem, Lemma 1, Theorem 2) with explicit rate sequences and non-identifiable class constructions.
XbQw70QBqD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that relaxing exact-support validity to sampling-based breadth and robustness with explicit quantifier rigor is a clean theoretical refinement.
XbQw70QBqD.main_concern: Reviewers note strong uniformity assumptions over target languages and distributions, limited novelty over Kalavasis et al. (2025, 2026), and no empirical validation on real LLMs.

UdgTkb5vfy.one_liner: Automates scraping jailbreak descriptions, synthesizing executable attack generators with an LLM, scoring guardrails, and sequentially fine-tuning WildGuard.
UdgTkb5vfy.problem: New jailbreak techniques appear faster than human engineers can reimplement them, build evaluation sets, and retrain LLM safety guardrails.
UdgTkb5vfy.method: RT-Agent scrapes candidate attack descriptions, uses a frontier LLM to synthesize and validate executable attack generators, evaluates them against four production guardrails, and sequentially fine-tunes the target guard on the discovered attacks in a closed loop.
UdgTkb5vfy.key_idea: Closes an automated red-teaming loop where an LLM converts scraped jailbreak descriptions into executable generators to continuously fine-tune guardrails.
UdgTkb5vfy.evidence: Processed 45,248 scraped documents, promoting 30 candidates into 7 working attacks (plus 6 curated strategies), evaluated on WildGuard and 5 standard safety benchmarks.
UdgTkb5vfy.claimed_gains: Synthesized attacks raise strict guard-jailbreak rate by up to 89.6 percentage points; sequential fine-tuning of WildGuard lowers average harmful pass-through from 20.3% to 1.6% (13x reduction).
UdgTkb5vfy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that automating end-to-end jailbreak extraction, generation, and guardrail adaptation addresses a practical engineering need.
UdgTkb5vfy.main_concern: Reviewers note insufficient baseline comparisons (only Rapid Response), lack of an ablation isolating feedback-based attack selection from fixed ordering, and example-based deduplication.

STYMZRz5yP.one_liner: Characterizes the worst-case multi-task regret-transfer distortion of a single proper scoring rule via decision-boundary curvature charges.
STYMZRz5yP.problem: Under model misspecification, minimizing one fixed proper scoring rule can yield suboptimal decisions across multiple downstream tasks with differing decision boundaries.
STYMZRz5yP.method: The authors reduce worst-case multi-task target-risk ratio to a pointwise two-sided divergence distortion, derive exact distortion bounds via curvature charges on decision facets, and compute optimal task-score weights via a covering LP.
STYMZRz5yP.key_idea: Reduces worst-case multi-task regret transfer under misspecification to pointwise divergence distortion governed by decision-boundary curvature charges.
STYMZRz5yP.evidence: Proves minimax, covering-LP, and kernel-smoothing theorems, validated on controlled synthetic studies, neural training, and weather prediction.
STYMZRz5yP.claimed_gains: Yields an exact distortion factor of m for an orthogonal family of m two-action tasks on K outcomes (m <= K-1).
STYMZRz5yP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the theoretical characterization via curvature charges and the covering-LP construction for optimal proper scores are mathematically rigorous.
STYMZRz5yP.main_concern: On real weather data, task-aware scores do not significantly outperform log loss, and the practical motivation for restricting to one fixed proper score is unclear.

AgVtCSanZ5.one_liner: Extracts activity-associated sparse features from ESM-2 cross-layer transcoders to guide active-learning candidate selection for protein optimization.
AgVtCSanZ5.problem: Active-learning protein optimization under scarce experimental measurements relies on fitness predictors without exploiting interpretable sparse representations inside protein language models.
AgVtCSanZ5.method: EvoCircuit extracts sparse features from ESM-2 cross-layer transcoders (CLTs), identifies features correlated with measured activity each round, and combines them with predictor-based ranking to acquire candidate variants.
AgVtCSanZ5.key_idea: Uses activity-correlated sparse features from ESM-2 cross-layer transcoders to guide active-learning acquisition alongside fitness predictors.
AgVtCSanZ5.evidence: Evaluated across 11 protein fitness landscapes (single-mutant, fixed-site, and variable-site libraries) and controlled feature-selection comparisons.
AgVtCSanZ5.claimed_gains: Outperforms predictor-only selection in 17 of 20 predictor-dataset comparisons on four variable-site libraries, including a 45.9% increase for FolDE on cgreGFP.
AgVtCSanZ5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that applying sparse mechanistic-interpretability features from pLMs to protein active learning is a creative, well-motivated direction.
AgVtCSanZ5.main_concern: Reported gains over strong predictors like FolDE are small or noisy with high variance, and the main text lacks a clear algorithmic explanation of CLT intervention.

IMy9ktSq0B.one_liner: Maintains coarse visual memory with a temporal router that dynamically retrieves fine-grained visual tokens during multi-step MLLM reasoning.
IMy9ktSq0B.problem: One-shot visual token compression fixes the visual context before decoding, failing when multi-step MLLM reasoning shifts which fine-grained visual details are needed.
IMy9ktSq0B.method: ViMoD uses Deformable Aggregation (DART) to build coarse visual tokens linked to recoverable fine tokens, and Temporal Routing (TRACE) to predict upcoming evidence needs from decoding history and swap active fine tokens.
IMy9ktSq0B.key_idea: Pairs adaptive coarse visual grouping (DART) with a temporal router (TRACE) that dynamically retrieves stage-specific fine tokens during decoding.
IMy9ktSq0B.evidence: Evaluated on eight multimodal reasoning benchmarks using Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct across token budgets, with ablations isolating DART and TRACE.
IMy9ktSq0B.claimed_gains: Leads all eight reasoning benchmarks at a 20% active visual-token budget.
IMy9ktSq0B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that addressing shifting visual evidence needs during multi-step reasoning is well motivated and supported by strong tight-budget scores.
IMy9ktSq0B.main_concern: ViMoD retains the full KV cache (increasing peak GPU memory), tests only Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, and uses decoding caps that may disproportionately truncate baselines.

Zu6HKmiROy.one_liner: Attenuates task-relevant LLM activations and patches normal-run states to separate answer recovery from activation-space proximity.
Zu6HKmiROy.problem: It remains unclear how disrupting internal task-relevant LLM activations affects reasoning and whether returning activations toward normal states equates to behavioral recovery.
Zu6HKmiROy.method: The authors gradually attenuate internal activations at task-relevant token positions, select intervention strengths from performance curves, and patch activations from correct or incorrect normal runs back into the perturbed model.
Zu6HKmiROy.key_idea: Compares activation writeback from correct versus incorrect normal runs after task-token attenuation to decouple behavioral recovery from activation proximity.
Zu6HKmiROy.evidence: Evaluated across five open-weight dense LLMs and four reasoning tasks with component-level attention and feed-forward analyses.
Zu6HKmiROy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that showing incorrect-source activations can reduce activation distance without restoring reasoning is a useful cautionary insight for activation patching.
Zu6HKmiROy.main_concern: Distance metrics rely on a 128D random projection without unprojected validation, and the core recovery-from-selected-sites behavior is expected.

URQZKM8CLa.one_liner: Formalizes unintended trait shifts during RL post-training using the evolutionary Price equation decomposed into selection and transmission.
URQZKM8CLa.problem: RL post-training with verifiable rewards can inadvertently amplify or suppress non-targeted behavioral traits and internal properties.
URQZKM8CLa.method: The authors derive a Price equation formalism for trait evolution under RL probability redistribution, decomposing trait changes into selection and transmission terms evaluated on GRPO-trained LLMs.
URQZKM8CLa.key_idea: Models non-targeted trait drift during RL post-training via the evolutionary Price equation's selection and transmission decomposition.
URQZKM8CLa.evidence: Evaluated on language models trained with GRPO across output-level and feature-level trait dynamics.
URQZKM8CLa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the Price equation provides a clean formal accounting framework whose predictions track sampled GRPO trait dynamics.
URQZKM8CLa.main_concern: The formalism is largely post-hoc accounting of expected spurious correlations without offering a principled mitigation or testing beyond controlled setups.

f8HuMKzsHf.one_liner: Applies adaptive token quantization and downstream utility adaptation on-device to limit image reconstruction leakage in split VLM inference.
f8HuMKzsHf.problem: Transmitting intermediate visual tokens in split VLM inference leaks private image content to reconstruction attacks, while prior defenses degrade task utility.
f8HuMKzsHf.method: UAQB deploys an on-device adaptive quantizer on visual tokens to bound image information flow via a tractable information bottleneck upper bound, paired with a utility adapter that restores compatibility with a frozen server-side VLM.
f8HuMKzsHf.key_idea: Jointly optimizing an on-device adaptive token quantizer and a utility adapter under a tractable information-bottleneck upper bound balances privacy and VLM accuracy.
f8HuMKzsHf.evidence: Evaluates multiple VLM utility benchmarks and adapted reconstruction attacks (e.g., LPIPS, OCR) alongside TrustCLIP checks.
f8HuMKzsHf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that split VLM privacy is a practical problem and that UAQB demonstrates a favorable empirical privacy-utility trade-off.
f8HuMKzsHf.main_concern: Reviewers note that sparsity (zero-index fraction) does not prove low representation entropy, attacker adaptation was capped at 10 epochs, and runtime was profiled on an H100 rather than edge devices.

jt2IDpyS7m.one_liner: Uses epoch-based deployment of stabilizing policies to prove online model-free Q-learning convergence in countably infinite state spaces.
jt2IDpyS7m.problem: Extending model-free Q-learning to countably infinite state spaces risks exploration-induced instability where the state drifts away and stalls learning.
jt2IDpyS7m.method: The authors propose an online, model-free Q-learning framework under discounted rewards that alternates exploratory policies with recurrent deployment of policies having controlled return times to a reference state. They establish asymptotic convergence using Robbins-Monro conditions and weighted norms for polynomially growing rewards.
jt2IDpyS7m.key_idea: An epoch-based exploration schedule periodically deploys strongly stabilizing policies to ensure recurrent visits to a reference state without truncating the state space.
jt2IDpyS7m.evidence: Theoretical convergence proofs (Theorems 3.1 and 4.1) and numerical examples comparing framework variants.
jt2IDpyS7m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize that the paper clearly identifies the exploration-drift problem in infinite state spaces and offers a structured framework with weighted-norm convergence under Robbins-Monro conditions.
jt2IDpyS7m.main_concern: One reviewer provides a counterexample claiming Theorem 4.1 is incorrect as stated, and others note strong, hard-to-verify assumptions on strongly stabilizing policies and lack of finite-time bounds.

3946pdjk7R.one_liner: Trains a compact state-affine latent dynamics model with multi-step rollout supervision to stabilize visual planning.
3946pdjk7R.problem: Joint-embedding world models trained on one-step errors suffer uncontrolled nonlinear error propagation during recursive visual planning rollouts.
3946pdjk7R.method: SALT parameterizes action-conditioned latent transitions as state-affine (state-independent Jacobians) so error propagation depends only on actions, and trains the transition recursively on multi-step predicted latent rollouts.
3946pdjk7R.key_idea: Restricts latent transitions to be state-affine with state-independent Jacobians and trains via recursive multi-step rollout loss to match planning-time usage.
3946pdjk7R.evidence: Evaluated across four visual planning environments including PushT, TwoRoom, and OGBench-Cube against LeWM and other world models.
3946pdjk7R.claimed_gains: Exhibits 1.48-2.19x higher one-step error than matched LeWM yet improves closed-loop planning success by 10.0 percentage points on average across four environments.
3946pdjk7R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the small, fast predictor (0.70M params, ~3x faster planning) and strong closed-loop gains despite higher one-step error.
3946pdjk7R.main_concern: Reviewers point out that ablations do not isolate the affine structure from rollout training (no small nonlinear rollout-trained control) and note discrepancies in Table 1 baselines.

xxyC5WkjEh.one_liner: Uses counterfactual role probes and activation patching to separate source-role readability from causal actionability in prompt injection.
xxyC5WkjEh.problem: Linear probes can decode instruction-versus-data source roles in LLM agents without identifying representation edits that causally alter tool execution.
xxyC5WkjEh.method: The authors apply counterfactual role probes, component-wise activation patching, and subspace interventions on matched-authorization pairs and AgentDojo trajectories. They test whether editing along role directions or removing channel subspaces changes tool calls and attack success.
xxyC5WkjEh.key_idea: Contrasts counterfactual role-probe decodability against causal activation patching and span-wide steering interventions along role directions during tool execution.
xxyC5WkjEh.evidence: Experiments on Qwen-2.5-7B, Llama 3.1, and Gemma 2 across matched-authorization pairs and AgentDojo trajectories.
xxyC5WkjEh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the careful counterfactual probe controls, component-wise interventions, and multi-condition AgentDojo evaluation.
xxyC5WkjEh.main_concern: Reviewers note that the tested 2024 models lack modern prompt-injection training, the readability-versus-causality gap is already known, and role decoding is only indirectly linked to IPI behavior.

P4erKj5EXN.one_liner: Releases differentially private PageRank scores and top-k lists under row-level privacy using degree-floored, mass-capped regularization.
P4erKj5EXN.problem: Standard edge-level differential privacy does not protect a node's entire outgoing-link profile when releasing PageRank scores or rankings.
P4erKj5EXN.method: The authors propose a regularized PageRank query combining degree flooring and source mass clipping to bound row-level sensitivity. DP PageRank-Score adds Gaussian noise for full scores, while DP PageRank-Top k uses Gumbel noise for ordered top-k recovery.
P4erKj5EXN.key_idea: Combines degree flooring and outgoing-mass clipping to bound global row-sensitivity for Gaussian full-score and Gumbel top-k PageRank release.
P4erKj5EXN.evidence: Minimax upper and lower bounds for dense graphs and numerical experiments on three real datasets and simulated networks.
P4erKj5EXN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the stronger row-level privacy model, clear sensitivity/bias analysis, and matching dense-graph minimax bounds.
P4erKj5EXN.main_concern: Reviewers note permissive privacy budgets (large epsilon, delta=0.1) in experiments and that the full-vector mechanism has higher overall L2 error than a uniform baseline.

q4tWsuruGG.one_liner: Builds longEM-IQA/Bench and EM-Lens to localize signal segments in long I/Q streams and measure parameters via DSP tools.
q4tWsuruGG.problem: Electromagnetic MLLMs only handle isolated short snippets and degrade when reasoning directly over long streams with multiple heterogeneous signal events.
q4tWsuruGG.method: They introduce longEM-IQA and longEM-Bench spanning 11 I/Q-language tasks across localization, identification, parameter estimation, and composite entities. EM-Lens actively localizes target segments within long observations, extracts physical parameters using explicit signal-processing tools, and uses hybrid training to balance active analysis with segment perception.
q4tWsuruGG.key_idea: Combines query-conditioned active segment localization with explicit DSP parameter-extraction tools and hybrid training for long I/Q stream understanding.
q4tWsuruGG.evidence: Evaluated on the simulated longEM-Bench suite across 11 I/Q-language tasks.
q4tWsuruGG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree moving from isolated signal snippets to long-observation I/Q understanding and combining localization with DSP tools is well-motivated.
q4tWsuruGG.main_concern: Reviewers unanimously criticize the lack of evaluation on real-world measured I/Q captures (e.g., EMRB), as both training and test data come from the authors' simulator.

WSVCIVl9n4.one_liner: Trains an RL orchestrator to selectively retrieve, apply, disregard, or propose reusable mathematical constraints during problem solving.
WSVCIVl9n4.problem: Mathematical reasoning LLMs violate critical solution constraints and lack mechanisms to selectively enforce or reuse them across trajectories.
WSVCIVl9n4.method: CROW formulates constraint utilization as a sequential decision-making problem where an RL-trained orchestrator retrieves, inspects, applies, or discards constraints based on downstream answer correctness. Constraints proposed during successful solutions are added back to an expanding constraint memory for future problems.
WSVCIVl9n4.key_idea: Optimizes an RL orchestrator to selectively retrieve, apply, ignore, or add reusable mathematical constraints to an expanding memory bank.
WSVCIVl9n4.evidence: Evaluated on HARDMath, HARDMath2, Calculus, Precalculus, and Algebra against multi-agent and search-based baselines, plus component ablations.
WSVCIVl9n4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree selectively gating constraint application avoids harming accuracy and yields large gains on HARDMath (30.84% vs. <=4.22%).
WSVCIVl9n4.main_concern: Reviewers note gains are concentrated almost exclusively on HARDMath while lagging on HARDMath2/Calculus, and ablations do not separate constraint value from ordinary training-problem retrieval.

N50ZtvHdp4.one_liner: Detects and steers spontaneous agent deception using sliding-window internal hidden states before decisive actions occur.
N50ZtvHdp4.problem: Existing agent monitoring detects deception only after it appears in observable actions or outputs.
N50ZtvHdp4.method: The paper aligns trajectories around behaviorally decisive steps, detects distributional shifts in pre-decision hidden states using Deep-Kernel MMD, and applies contrastive activation steering to reduce deceptive outcomes.
N50ZtvHdp4.key_idea: Applies Deep-Kernel MMD to sliding-window hidden states prior to decisive agent steps to predict and steer away from spontaneous deception.
N50ZtvHdp4.evidence: Experiments across five failure scenarios using 2,000 trajectories from Qwen3-14B.
N50ZtvHdp4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value reframing deception monitoring from post-hoc output auditing to pre-behavioral internal-state prediction.
N50ZtvHdp4.main_concern: Reviewers warn that honest vs. deceptive labels are confounded with task failure/uncertainty, temporal claims are confounded with varying cohort lengths, and experiments use only Qwen3-14B.

ZbeW3SJ7wx.one_liner: Aligns the spectral-context branch of a compact dual-branch U-Net bottleneck with a pretrained spectral neural operator in frequency space.
ZbeW3SJ7wx.problem: Compact convolutional encoder-decoders for onboard sparse physical field reconstruction lack field-wide context in their capacity-constrained bottlenecks.
ZbeW3SJ7wx.method: SS-REPA splits the bottleneck into a mean-shift spatial branch and a spectral-context branch, aligning only the spectral branch's real and imaginary frequency components to a pretrained spectral neural operator via a Gaussian-weighted low-frequency loss.
ZbeW3SJ7wx.key_idea: Separates spatial detail from spectral context in a compact U-Net bottleneck and aligns the spectral branch to a pretrained neural operator in frequency space.
ZbeW3SJ7wx.evidence: Evaluated on three sparse-sensor physical field benchmarks and profiled on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano edge device.
ZbeW3SJ7wx.claimed_gains: Achieves competitive accuracy with ~94% fewer parameters (0.86M vs. 13.39M) and 83.3-85.5% lower inference latency than the standard U-Net baseline.
ZbeW3SJ7wx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical onboard edge-device motivation backed by real Orin Nano latency measurements and detailed ablations.
ZbeW3SJ7wx.main_concern: Reviewers note that the 94% parameter and 84% latency gains compare a 0.86M compact U-Net against a 13.39M standard U-Net, lack feature-distillation baselines, and reduce mathematically to simple spatial 1x1 convolutions.

WzglaHasZj.one_liner: Replaces quadratic moment matrices with linear lag-profile summaries for one-shot analytic federated time-series forecasting and local adaptation.
WzglaHasZj.problem: One-shot analytic federated forecasting transmits quadratic moment matrices and lacks client-specific adaptation without extra communication rounds.
WzglaHasZj.method: FedTinyTS exchanges compact O(L+H) lag-profile summaries in a single round for reliability-aware analytic ridge fitting of a channel-independent linear forecaster, then personalizes locally using retained client moments.
WzglaHasZj.key_idea: Compresses quadratic temporal moment matrices into O(L+H) lag profiles for one-shot analytic aggregation followed by zero-communication local personalization.
WzglaHasZj.evidence: Evaluated across five benchmarks (up to 862 clients) and four forecasting horizons against FedAvg and dense FedRidge.
WzglaHasZj.claimed_gains: Reduces message payload by up to 8,548x over FedAvg and up to 90.7x over dense FedRidge while lowering global MSE vs. FedAvg on four of five benchmarks.
WzglaHasZj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the O(L+H) one-shot communication reduction and the large-client benchmark evaluation with zero-communication personalization.
WzglaHasZj.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the simulator computes personalization server-side with dense moments in memory, omits matched-budget compressed FedRidge baselines, and shows weak MAE performance.

jthYFq8ydb.one_liner: Composes multi-entity visual cue maps on the original image grid before cropping to preserve relational context in LVLMs.
jthYFq8ydb.problem: Crop-before-compose inference methods discard relational context between entities or introduce visual clutter when selecting crops for fine-grained LVLM reasoning.
jthYFq8ydb.method: PostCrop localizes queried entities, composes their bidirectional cue maps on the original visual grid, and adaptively selects the surrounding context region before forming the final crop without training.
jthYFq8ydb.key_idea: Composes multi-entity localization cue maps on the original image grid to adaptively select relational context before cropping.
jthYFq8ydb.evidence: Controlled context-variation diagnostics and evaluations across HR-Bench-4K, HR-Bench-8K, VSTAR, and TreeBench.
jthYFq8ydb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean diagnostic characterization of the entity-context trade-off and consistent empirical improvements across benchmarks.
jthYFq8ydb.main_concern: Adaptive crop selection adds small gains over a fixed union crop, inference requires high latency/multiple forward passes, and novelty over attention-cropping works is limited.

vEidVHeOg4.one_liner: Approximates factor-to-variable messages directly under Dirac-input consistency to replace iterative expectation propagation with a single sweep.
vEidVHeOg4.problem: Expectation propagation and variational message passing approximate edge marginals, requiring iterative schedules and risking negative-precision messages or point-estimate collapse.
vEidVHeOg4.method: Direct Message Approximation (DMA) constructs factor-to-variable messages directly using a Dirac-input consistency condition and derives explicit updates for product and leaky-ReLU factors. Assembled into a Bayesian neural network inference algorithm, it performs one forward/backward sweep per example without a gradient learning-rate hyperparameter.
vEidVHeOg4.key_idea: Directly approximates factor-to-variable messages under Dirac-delta input consistency, bounding local marginal KL by message KL without EP inner-loop iterations.
vEidVHeOg4.evidence: Proves local marginal KL and O(1/r^2) product-factor bounds and evaluates a DMA-based BNN on synthetic regression tasks with up to 52K weights.
vEidVHeOg4.claimed_gains: Proves an O(1/r^2) guarantee for the product factor backward message and scales BNN inference to synthetic regression tasks of up to 52K weights.
vEidVHeOg4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly motivates and structures direct message approximation as a clean alternative to EP and VMP.
vEidVHeOg4.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about theory-to-appendix mismatches, unaddressed small-SNR regimes, missing prior belief-propagation context, and incomplete Bayesian baselines.

8nOrTTgvwo.one_liner: Pretrains a Level-3 limit order book transformer with aggregate activity forecasting and masked message modeling for low-label transfer.
8nOrTTgvwo.problem: End-to-end limit order book forecasting models require substantial labeled data and fail to transfer across assets or tasks in low-data regimes.
8nOrTTgvwo.method: LOBRE tokenizes irregular Nasdaq Level-3 messages one event per token and pretrains a transformer encoder jointly with masked message modeling (MMM) and Aggregate Activity Forecasting (AAF). AAF supervises the pooled sequence representation to predict future order-flow aggregates so a frozen encoder adapts via small task heads.
8nOrTTgvwo.key_idea: Combines masked message modeling with label-free Aggregate Activity Forecasting on pooled representations of irregular Level-3 message-token sequences.
8nOrTTgvwo.evidence: Evaluated on four short-horizon tasks with 1 and 15 days of labels across six pretraining, six held-out, and six cross-sector Nasdaq assets.
8nOrTTgvwo.claimed_gains: LOBRE improves on the same transformer trained from scratch by a mean of 0.049 Macro-F1 across twelve assets and +0.049 Macro-F1 on six additional cross-sector assets tested six months later.
8nOrTTgvwo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the controlled comparison against an identical randomly initialized architecture clearly isolates cross-asset transfer gains from pretraining.
8nOrTTgvwo.main_concern: Reviewers note weak or collapsing scratch/fine-tuned baselines, close alignment between AAF targets and downstream tasks, and missing AAF-only ablations.

Nim9ZlB2Tu.one_liner: Benchmarks multimodal visual agents on 223 real-world 3D Blender creation tasks using multi-view rendering and 2,651 binary rubrics.
Nim9ZlB2Tu.problem: Existing 3D agent benchmarks lack coverage of realistic, open-ended 3D modeling and editing workflows driven by diverse multimodal references.
Nim9ZlB2Tu.method: BlenderWorld comprises 223 tasks across architecture, products, natural environments, and scientific visualization from text, image, video, and structured specs. Submitted Blender projects are rendered from multiple viewpoints and scored by a VLM judge against 2,651 task-specific binary rubrics, native scene checks, and holistic visual quality.
Nim9ZlB2Tu.key_idea: Evaluates autonomous 3D Blender agents by combining multi-view rendered VLM-judge scoring, native scene inspection, and 2,651 task-specific binary rubrics.
Nim9ZlB2Tu.evidence: Benchmarks 13 frontier models across 223 tasks with human-preference correlation checks on the VLM judge.
Nim9ZlB2Tu.claimed_gains: Across 13 frontier models, GPT-6-Astra achieves the highest overall fused score of 79.9, followed by Opus-5 (73.0) and GPT-5.6-Sol (67.7).
Nim9ZlB2Tu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree BlenderWorld addresses a timely gap with realistic 3D creation tasks, native project inspection, and broad frontier-model evaluation.
Nim9ZlB2Tu.main_concern: Reviewers question the reliability of relying on a single VLM judge for rubric and dimension scoring and view the contribution as more engineering than methodological.

HVB4ph8OVJ.one_liner: Maintains a constant-factor approximation for fully dynamic regularized submodular maximization with polylogarithmic amortized query complexity.
HVB4ph8OVJ.problem: Existing fully dynamic submodular algorithms require nonnegative objectives, while regularized submodular algorithms do not support arbitrary element deletions.
HVB4ph8OVJ.method: BatchReg uses joint cost-gain bucketing and filtered batch selection to handle both insertions and deletions under a cardinality constraint for potentially negative regularized submodular objectives.
HVB4ph8OVJ.key_idea: Combines joint cost-gain bucketing with filtered batch selection to maintain regularized submodular solutions under arbitrary insertions and deletions.
HVB4ph8OVJ.evidence: Theoretical approximation and query complexity proofs plus maximum-coverage experiments on one real-world graph.
HVB4ph8OVJ.claimed_gains: Achieves a (3 - sqrt(5))/2 - epsilon approximation ratio using poly(log n, log k, 1/epsilon) expected amortized oracle queries per update.
HVB4ph8OVJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper fills a theoretical gap by achieving a constant-factor guarantee with polylogarithmic amortized queries for dynamic regularized submodular maximization.
HVB4ph8OVJ.main_concern: Reviewers find the conceptual novelty modest over prior streaming work and criticize the experiments as preliminary (single graph, baselines restarting on every deletion, no wall-clock timings).

HcKDYJ7cxV.one_liner: Integrates 80+ drug-discovery tools with an experience-driven conditional skill library reviewed by an independent agent.
HcKDYJ7cxV.problem: Computational drug-discovery agents struggle to coordinate specialized tools and reuse execution experience reliably across evolving evidence.
HcKDYJ7cxV.method: DrugHarness combines over 80 scientific operations and executable code with a self-evolving skill system that distills execution traces into skills with explicit applicability conditions. An independent review agent validates candidate skills against evidence and targeted trials before admitting them to guide future tasks.
HcKDYJ7cxV.key_idea: Distills drug-discovery execution experience into skills with explicit applicability conditions, vetted by an independent review agent before reuse.
HcKDYJ7cxV.evidence: Evaluated on MolBench (affinity comparison, molecular editing), development tasks with Qwen, and wet-lab synthesis/testing for an HPK1 inhibitor.
HcKDYJ7cxV.claimed_gains: Achieves 91.9% affinity-comparison and 100% molecular-editing accuracy on MolBench without evolution, 81.1% vs. 62.2% on Qwen dev tasks, and 14.19 nM vs. 37.47 nM cellular IC50 on HPK1.
HcKDYJ7cxV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree separating source observations from conditional skills and testing across diverse tasks (including wet-lab HPK1 validation) is well-structured.
HcKDYJ7cxV.main_concern: Reviewers highlight that headline cross-system comparisons confound the harness with different LLM backbones (e.g., GPT-5.6 Terra vs. Sonnet 4.6) and retrospective evolution tests.

YpL4lsNANl.one_liner: Diagnoses agent memory failures via interventional tracing (MemPath) and aligns retrieval with typed question demands (BiDE-Mem).
YpL4lsNANl.problem: Item-level retrieval relevance in agent memory systems fails to guarantee set-level evidential sufficiency required to answer complex multi-hop or temporal questions.
YpL4lsNANl.method: The authors introduce MemPath, an interventional diagnostic framework tracing memory lifecycles across access, demand coverage, and evidence utilization. Guided by it, BiDE-Mem decomposes questions into typed demands, retrieves across multiple channels, and organizes demand-relevant support relationships prior to answering.
YpL4lsNANl.key_idea: Diagnoses memory bottlenecks via lifecycle interventions and decomposes questions into typed demands to guide multi-channel retrieval and evidence organization.
YpL4lsNANl.evidence: Evaluated on LoCoMo and LongMemEval against representative memory systems under shared reader models and component ablations.
YpL4lsNANl.claimed_gains: Improves LoCoMo accuracy by 6.23 points and reaches 91.80% overall accuracy on LongMemEval.
YpL4lsNANl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree MemPath provides a useful diagnostic separation between memory accessibility, demand coverage, and evidence utilization.
YpL4lsNANl.main_concern: Reviewers note incomplete pipeline specifications, missing latency/cost accounting for multi-channel retrieval and LLM reranking, and confounded ablations and figure counts.

y5tu2f3qLD.one_liner: Jointly selects an action chunk and dynamic execution horizon for VLA policies using sensitivity to initial noise perturbations.
y5tu2f3qLD.problem: Fixed-horizon action chunking in VLA models faces a trade-off between frequent expensive policy calls and imprecise open-loop execution over long horizons.
y5tu2f3qLD.method: PICES is a training-free inference method that generates a batch of action chunks from multiple initial noise samples and locally perturbed counterparts in one policy call. It measures action sensitivity between nominal and perturbed chunks to set candidate-specific execution horizons and picks the chunk with the longest reliable horizon.
y5tu2f3qLD.key_idea: Generates nominal and noise-perturbed action chunks in one call, using their divergence to select the chunk and its dynamic execution horizon.
y5tu2f3qLD.evidence: Evaluated on simulation benchmarks (SimplerEnv, LIBERO) and real-world robot manipulation tasks on Jetson Orin and Thor.
y5tu2f3qLD.claimed_gains: Achieves up to 2.3x wall-clock policy inference speedup on Jetson Orin and Thor relative to baselines.
y5tu2f3qLD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the training-free perturbation-sensitivity mechanism is simple, intuitive, and accounts for its own batching overhead on Jetson hardware.
y5tu2f3qLD.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical benefit under asynchronous execution (like RTC), note PICES still requires tuning a minimum horizon, and point out missing sensitivity-metric ablations.

TwMgB1qo1g.one_liner: Introduces TieDPO, a margin-regularized DPO objective, plus MultiTie-22k and TieBench-MI for tied multi-image MLLM preferences.
TwMgB1qo1g.problem: Standard preference optimization forces tied multi-image MLLM responses into strict binary labels, inducing verbosity, position, and evidence-path biases.
TwMgB1qo1g.method: The authors formalize four tie categories, construct the ternary-labeled MultiTie-22k dataset and TieBench-MI benchmark (2,400 pairs), and propose TieDPO, which applies standard DPO on strict pairs while regularizing tied pairs toward indifference via a margin-based penalty.
TwMgB1qo1g.key_idea: Preserves standard DPO on strict preference pairs while adding a margin-based indifference regularizer for tied multi-image preference pairs.
TwMgB1qo1g.evidence: Evaluated on two MLLM backbones (including Qwen3-VL) across seven multi-image and single-image benchmarks plus TieBench-MI.
TwMgB1qo1g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree handling tied preferences is practical and MultiTie-22k and TieBench-MI are useful resources for multi-image alignment.
TwMgB1qo1g.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over prior tie-aware DPO methods (e.g., Davidson-DPO, TODO) and unsubstantiated claims that ties are uniquely amplified in multi-image settings.

1FkKvXT8KI.one_liner: Fuses atomic-memory and direct-turn retrieval with source resolution and conservative conflict-based refusal for conversational memory.
1FkKvXT8KI.problem: Conversational memory systems confuse retrieval relevance with evidential sufficiency, answering from mismatched participants/times or refusing poorly.
1FkKvXT8KI.method: GroundedMem indexes histories as compact atomic memories, fuses atomic and direct-turn retrieval via RRF reranking, and resolves candidates back to complete source turns. A verifier refuses only when constrained frame-mismatch checks fire without detected support, leaving unresolved cases on the answer path.
1FkKvXT8KI.key_idea: Resolves fused atomic/turn retrieval back to full source turns and restricts refusal to verified frame mismatches without supporting evidence.
1FkKvXT8KI.evidence: Evaluated on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S with paired answer-model/judge comparisons and refusal F1 metrics.
1FkKvXT8KI.claimed_gains: Improves LoCoMo LLM-judge accuracy by 7.75 points, LongMemEval-S accuracy by 3.4 points, and LoCoMo refusal F1 by 18.13 points over REMem.
1FkKvXT8KI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree separating retrieval relevance from evidential sufficiency and preserving source-turn provenance are clear, useful contributions.
1FkKvXT8KI.main_concern: Reviewers find the novelty low (combining existing RRF, atomic memory, and prompted-LLM verification) and note that source restoration itself is not directly ablated.

fYSgw6SoQk.one_liner: Benchmarks persistent coding agents as dynamic workload managers executing arriving task streams under shared CPU and memory limits.
fYSgw6SoQk.problem: Existing coding-agent benchmarks evaluate tasks one at a time and fail to measure whether agents can schedule and deliver concurrent arriving workloads under shared compute limits.
fYSgw6SoQk.method: AOS-Bench runs persistent model–harness systems on isolated, streaming, and burst task workloads under shared CPU and memory constraints, tracking task intake, concurrency, claim latency, and workload delivery across execution policies.
fYSgw6SoQk.key_idea: Shifts coding-agent evaluation from single tasks to timed arriving streams under shared host limits, measuring intake collapse and throughput across scheduling policies.
fYSgw6SoQk.evidence: Supported by evaluations of five model–harness pairs across isolated, stream, and burst workloads on a 4-CPU, 8 GB memory machine.
fYSgw6SoQk.claimed_gains: Systems differing by 13 percentage points in isolated success differ by 29 points in medium stream success; on heavy workloads, two systems with identical isolated baselines deliver 72.2% vs. 49.7%, while serial dispatch leaves 73% unclaimed and no policy exceeds 30% CPU utilization.
fYSgw6SoQk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree evaluating persistent agents on multi-task workloads rather than single tasks is timely and cleanly reveals intake-collapse failures.
fYSgw6SoQk.main_concern: Reviewers flag a mismatch in task-exclusion rules (filtering per-system nonzero baselines in Table 2), narrow evaluation on a single under-stressed 4-CPU/8 GB host, and vague workload generation details.

NLO2RmSOiX.one_liner: Learns uncertainty-aware causal treatment policies by maximizing posterior mean welfare plus lower-tail CVaR over Bayesian-bootstrap and nuisance draws.
NLO2RmSOiX.problem: Empirical welfare maximization in causal policy learning can select treatment rules with high point-estimated welfare but severe downside estimation uncertainty.
NLO2RmSOiX.method: CUBO pairs common Bayesian-bootstrap weights with whole-function draws from a nuisance posterior to induce a joint welfare posterior across candidate policies, then maximizes a combination of posterior mean welfare and lower-tail conditional value-at-risk (CVaR).
NLO2RmSOiX.key_idea: Induces a joint policy-welfare posterior from shared Bayesian-bootstrap weights and nuisance-posterior draws, optimizing a mean-plus-lower-tail CVaR objective.
NLO2RmSOiX.evidence: Supported by finite-draw welfare regret bounds and experiments on IHDP and ACIC causal benchmarks.
