NLO2RmSOiX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree targeting aggregate policy-level welfare uncertainty with common posterior scenarios and CVaR is coherent and backed by careful regret theory.
NLO2RmSOiX.main_concern: Reviewers note that ablations do not isolate the CVaR objective from the Bayesian nuisance model, evaluations report single-instance averages rather than downside failure rates, and differences from BROIL/PG-BROIL need clearer positioning.

mqRcgatuvb.one_liner: Ranks diseases from sparse clinical intakes using a ternary evidence log, temporal-statistics predicates, and information-gain question selection.
mqRcgatuvb.problem: Sequential diagnostic pipelines suffer from unverifiable free-form reasoning, unnamed numerical trend descriptions, and negative bias from treating unasked findings as absent.
mqRcgatuvb.method: COTCAgent couples a Temporal-Statistics Adapter (turning irregular lab series into typed predicates) with a learnable knowledge-base energy over a ternary (present/absent/unknown) evidence log where unknown findings contribute zero energy, selecting follow-up questions by surrogate entropy reduction.
mqRcgatuvb.key_idea: Maintains a ternary present/absent/unknown evidence log scored by a listwise-trained knowledge-base energy (zero energy for unknown) to choose follow-up questions via surrogate entropy reduction.
mqRcgatuvb.evidence: Supported by sequential diagnosis experiments under matched question budgets on DDXPlus and MIMIC-IV.
mqRcgatuvb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree distinguishing unknown from absent findings under a limited diagnostic question budget is practically important and yields strong hit rates with few questions.
mqRcgatuvb.main_concern: Reviewers note missing ablations isolating the ternary representation and Temporal-Statistics Adapter, uncontrolled external baseline comparisons using different rankers, and dense method terminology.

C1D0ByaRyi.one_liner: Uses coding agents offline to compile visual-control tasks into frozen state-centric specialists with modular encoder, state, and policy interfaces.
C1D0ByaRyi.problem: Using general-purpose coding agents as online visual controllers requires repeated model calls per episode, causing high latency and inference cost.
C1D0ByaRyi.method: State-Centric Task Compilation (SCTC) concentrates coding-agent computation at development time to synthesize reusable frozen specialists structured into a visual encoder E, a task-state/memory module Z, and a control policy P, enabling localized recompilation of individual modules.
C1D0ByaRyi.key_idea: Compiles visual-control specifications into frozen standalone programs factorized into visual encoder, persistent task-state, and control-policy modules for fast execution and localized repair.
C1D0ByaRyi.evidence: Supported by evaluations on Craftax, object pushing (with visual perturbations and unseen shapes), and Minecraft.
C1D0ByaRyi.claimed_gains: In Craftax, a compiled specialist matches direct Astra mean reward with about 70x shorter episode runtime.
C1D0ByaRyi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree decoupling offline controller synthesis from online execution yields compelling runtime speedups and clean encoder-only repair on object pushing.
C1D0ByaRyi.main_concern: Reviewers question methodological novelty over prior agent-generated skill/controller methods (such as RHO and agentic Push-T), note missing ablations isolating the Z–E–P structure, and flag omitted compilation costs.

3WPx8rphhq.one_liner: Augments token-level knowledge distillation with a Cauchy–Schwarz divergence between teacher and student mixtures of teacher-derived token context distributions.
3WPx8rphhq.problem: Standard token-level distillation penalizes probability mismatches uniformly across vocabulary tokens without accounting for how the teacher relates those tokens across contexts.
3WPx8rphhq.method: Residual Composition Distillation (RCD) represents each vocabulary token by a teacher-derived distribution over contexts, forms teacher and student mixtures of these context distributions at each position, and adds their Cauchy–Schwarz divergence to standard probability-matching loss.
3WPx8rphhq.key_idea: Compares teacher and student next-token distributions by weighting teacher-derived per-token context distributions and minimizing their Cauchy–Schwarz divergence alongside standard token matching.
3WPx8rphhq.evidence: Supported by distillation experiments across two teacher–student language model families and multiple evaluation sets.
3WPx8rphhq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation for context-aware probability redistribution is clear and that the Cauchy–Schwarz context-mixture objective is principled and easy to plug into token distillation.
3WPx8rphhq.main_concern: Reviewers note that generation quality consistently degrades despite prediction and diversity gains, experiments use only two small model families, and context similarity is not justified over embedding or logit similarity.

ISfmyOapv7.one_liner: Coordinates parallel LLM principle-evolution branches via value-of-information-gated routing and context-discounted likelihood evidence injection.
ISfmyOapv7.problem: Sequential principle-evolution loops for LLM scientific discovery limit exploration breadth and waste wall-clock time on hard problems.
ISfmyOapv7.method: CoEvolve runs parallel principle-evolution branches with separate posteriors coordinated by a core that routes shared experimental measurements using value-of-information gating and injects them via context-discounted likelihood updates.
ISfmyOapv7.key_idea: Routes measurements across parallel principle-evolution branches using value-of-information gating and updates target branch posteriors via context-discounted likelihood injection.
ISfmyOapv7.evidence: Supported by transfer theory and budget-matched evaluations across six scientific-discovery tasks and five autonomous-research tasks on two LLM backbones (including GPT-5.6-Terra).
ISfmyOapv7.claimed_gains: Attains 66.5% mean solution quality vs. 57.0% for single-branch principle evolution with a 1.80x mean wall-clock speedup on GPT-5.6-Terra across six scientific-discovery tasks.
ISfmyOapv7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the VoI-gated evidence-routing mechanism is well motivated and backed by multi-task scientific and autonomous-research benchmarks.
ISfmyOapv7.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about reliance on surrogate scores without independent validation, missing domain-specific optimization and fixed-discount baselines, and poor readability including an unclear definition of evidence transfer.

dpOucEjdnF.one_liner: Infers per-agent rewards offline from continuous multi-agent demonstrations using belief-conditioned successor features, inverse TD consistency, and noise-contrastive estimation.
dpOucEjdnF.problem: Existing multi-agent IRL methods require online environment interaction, inner policy-optimization loops, or discrete actions, preventing offline reward inference on continuous social-behavior datasets.
dpOucEjdnF.method: MA-UITD represents each agent's unilateral long-term action consequences via belief-conditioned successor features marginalized over other agents, linking shared reward features and agent preference vectors through inverse temporal-difference consistency and noise-contrastive behavioral learning.
dpOucEjdnF.key_idea: Combines opponent-marginalized belief-conditioned successor features with inverse TD consistency and noise-contrastive estimation to infer explicit per-agent rewards offline in continuous-action spaces.
dpOucEjdnF.evidence: Supported by simulated cooperative, competitive, and general-sum benchmarks (including Simple Push and Gems) and a real mouse social-behavior dataset.
dpOucEjdnF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree offline explicit reward inference in continuous multi-agent settings is well motivated for behavioral neuroscience and combines successor features with NCE cleanly.
dpOucEjdnF.main_concern: Reviewers note weak continuous-action empirical evidence with no continuous-action baselines and mixed reward correlations, alongside incremental novelty over prior ITD and MAMQL formulations.

I9wq5SAYjk.one_liner: Preserves subject identity in visual autoregressive models via training-free source K/V sharing, band-selective RoPE phase rewinding, and residual-stream mixing.
I9wq5SAYjk.problem: Sharing coarse-scale source features for subject-consistent generation in next-scale visual autoregressive models inadvertently copies the source pose and spatial layout.
I9wq5SAYjk.method: SPIN records subject features in one unmodified source pass and injects them during target generation by restricting shared source K/V attention across scales, selectively rewinding high-frequency rotary phases to reduce positional bias, and mixing source and target residual layer updates.
I9wq5SAYjk.key_idea: Combines scale-aware source K/V attention sharing, high-frequency RoPE phase rewinding to remove positional bias, and residual-stream update mixing without training.
I9wq5SAYjk.evidence: Supported by factorial ablations, mechanism analyses, a user study, and evaluations across 191 prompt groups and five next-scale visual autoregressive backbones (including Infinity-2B).
I9wq5SAYjk.claimed_gains: On Infinity-2B at matched DreamSim of 0.18, retains higher centroid diversity than Infinite Story across three seeds (0.0913 vs. 0.0793); on the 191-group benchmark, lowers DreamSim from 0.235 to 0.182 vs. vanilla Infinity-2B while retaining 89% of pose diversity.
I9wq5SAYjk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree analyzing VAR scale boundaries and high-frequency RoPE positional bias is insightful, with band-selective RoPE rewind well supported by measurement.
I9wq5SAYjk.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the heavy hand-tuned complexity across three modules and question whether SPIN genuinely improves the identity–diversity Pareto frontier rather than shifting along it or generalizing across styles and backbones.

5GqpoBWlu3.one_liner: Tokenizes molecular graphs using byte-triple merge rules with canonical merged subgraphs and spectral positional encodings.
5GqpoBWlu3.problem: SMILES BPE is sensitive to enumeration order, while pair-based molecular graph tokenization (GraphBPE) conflates different merged connectivities and loses atom-level positions.
5GqpoBWlu3.method: GraphBTE defines each merge rule as a triple of two adjacent tokens plus the canonical representation of their merged subgraph, and adds spectral positional encoding (SPE) to preserve atom-level positions for downstream Transformer or GNN prediction.
5GqpoBWlu3.key_idea: Augment graph BPE merge rules with the canonical merged subgraph to disambiguate connectivity and inject spectral positional encodings for atom-level structure.
5GqpoBWlu3.evidence: Experiments evaluate GraphBTE across seven MoleculeNet classification datasets against GraphBPE and SMILES BPE, plus enumeration-invariance and vocabulary-size analyses.
5GqpoBWlu3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adding canonical merged subgraphs to graph BPE rules is a simple, well-motivated fix for connectivity ambiguity evaluated across seven MoleculeNet benchmarks.
5GqpoBWlu3.main_concern: Reviewers note inadequate baseline controls (SPE not given to baselines, missing MiCaM comparison), ablations suggesting SPE drives most gains rather than the merges, and remaining order-dependent tokenization ambiguity.

r54yCiXOr6.one_liner: Forecasts multi-step dynamics on evolving graphs by splitting persistent/arriving node handling and separating predictive and context cues.
r54yCiXOr6.problem: Most spatio-temporal graph forecasters assume fixed node sets and connectivity, failing when infrastructure nodes arrive, depart, or change topology without retraining.
r54yCiXOr6.method: DyCSTA retains history for persistent nodes, initializes newly arriving nodes from current observations, reconstructs graph dependencies, splits representations into main predictive and auxiliary context cues, and regularizes context conditioning via a replacement branch during training.
r54yCiXOr6.key_idea: Handle node arrivals and departures by combining persistent-node retention with current-window initialization and a regularized split between main predictive and auxiliary latent-context cues.
r54yCiXOr6.evidence: Experiments evaluate multi-step forecasting under changing node sets and new-node arrival on traffic, communication, and other evolving graph datasets (including PEMS-Stream, JiNan, Air-Stream, Energy-Stream).
r54yCiXOr6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate jointly tackling node arrivals, departures, and topology changes in multi-step forecasting with strong performance on evolving flow datasets.
r54yCiXOr6.main_concern: Reviewers flag potential test-set leakage in the stability-aware node selection distributions, a mismatch between the paper's Wasserstein ranking and the released code, and heavy overlap with CaST's representation decomposition.

4PczWoMYaa.one_liner: Maintains non-destructive, provenance-ordered agent memory that demotes rather than erases superseded facts under a single governor.
4PczWoMYaa.problem: Agent memory systems either fail to identify current values (retrieval stores), lose displaced history (summary stores), or ignore source provenance when resolving conflicting updates.
4PczWoMYaa.method: FactTrace organizes each attribute under a single knowledge-equilibration governor that absorbs compatible facts, demotes superseded values with full provenance and replacement history, and enforces a source-type trust order preventing lower-provenance claims from overriding verified facts.
4PczWoMYaa.key_idea: Maintain lifecycle-typed agent memory where conflicting facts demote prior values instead of deleting them and a source-provenance trust order governs which value is current.
4PczWoMYaa.evidence: Evaluations test FactTrace on two benchmarks: AMemGym for personal state tracking and AI-LieDar for truthfulness under user social pressure, with per-period and retrieval ablations.
4PczWoMYaa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating current facts, historical facts, and inferences with explicit provenance tracking is a practical design with positive benchmark results.
4PczWoMYaa.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns that headline truthfulness gains may be confounded by an explicit honesty response prompt not given to baselines, and note limited novelty over existing temporal/versioned memory systems (A-MEM, Mem0, Zep/Graphiti).

wEXgi16GVJ.one_liner: Bounds feed-forward visual SLAM memory via test-time self-supervised submap retrieval and lightweight terminal boundary re-inference.
wEXgi16GVJ.problem: Feed-forward visual geometry SLAM models incur memory and compute costs that grow unboundedly with sequence length when attending to full frame history.
wEXgi16GVJ.method: SMART-SLAM processes fixed-length submaps, selects only the most relevant past submaps as active history using a test-time self-supervised retrieval mechanism, and performs lightweight terminal backbone re-inference at submap boundaries to reduce accumulated drift.
wEXgi16GVJ.key_idea: Use fixed-length submaps with test-time self-supervised retrieval to bound active history and apply lightweight terminal re-inference across submap boundaries to correct drift.
wEXgi16GVJ.evidence: Evaluations measure speed, GPU memory, and accuracy across KITTI and indoor/outdoor SLAM datasets with retrieval and terminal-correction ablations.
wEXgi16GVJ.claimed_gains: Compared with baseline on KITTI sequences, SMART-SLAM runs online inference 2.5-3.9x faster and uses 57-61% less GPU memory.
wEXgi16GVJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling long-term submap storage from bounded active context directly addresses the memory and speed bottleneck of feed-forward SLAM transformers.
wEXgi16GVJ.main_concern: Reviewers cite incomplete specification of the local-to-global frame handoff, unisolated online-adaptation gains, reliance on conventional PGO for global loop closure, and dense presentation.

v7YYhqbSo3.one_liner: Separates a pointwise XYZ spatial tower from a geometry-guided multiscale RGB context tower for 3D robot manipulation policies.
v7YYhqbSo3.problem: Jointly encoding XYZ and RGB at each point degrades precise spatial manipulation, while separate pointwise encoding misses neighborhood appearance context.
v7YYhqbSo3.method: GeoRGB uses Asymmetric Dual-Tower Encoding (ADTE) to pair an independent pointwise XYZ pathway with a multiscale RGB hierarchy where Geometry-Guided RGB Contextualization (GRC) aggregates neighboring appearance features using XYZ neighborhoods and relative-position directional weights.
v7YYhqbSo3.key_idea: Keep pointwise XYZ spatial encoding separate from a multiscale RGB hierarchy that aggregates neighborhood color features using XYZ-defined directional weights before fusion.
v7YYhqbSo3.evidence: Evaluations span 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, 48 MetaWorld tasks, and four real-world manipulation tasks with modality and backbone ablations.
v7YYhqbSo3.claimed_gains: GeoRGB achieves 77.5% average success across 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks (+14.3 percentage points over the strongest baseline), 93.8% across four real-world tasks, and 75.0% on MetaWorld with fewer than half the parameters and under one-quarter the training time.
v7YYhqbSo3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that preserving exact XYZ geometry while contextualizing RGB cues is well motivated and achieves strong empirical results on RoboTwin and real-world tasks.
v7YYhqbSo3.main_concern: Reviewers note missing ablations comparing the learned XYZ tower against simple raw-XYZ concatenation, inconsistent gains on MetaWorld, unspecified GRC kernel-point configurations, and limited novelty over prior RGB-point-cloud fusion works.

fKqAUz2ItR.one_liner: Re-evaluates multi-turn tasks with each prior assistant turn isolated individually alongside all user turns, then votes on answers.
fKqAUz2ItR.problem: In multi-turn conversations where task requirements arrive gradually, early mistaken assistant responses remain in context and derail later answers even after full specifications are given.
fKqAUz2ItR.method: Isolated Consistency (IC) is a training-free inference method that generates one candidate answer per earlier assistant turn—conditioning each candidate on all user messages, a clean recap, and only that single assistant turn while masking all others—and aggregates answers by voting.
fKqAUz2ItR.key_idea: Generate one candidate per prior assistant turn by masking all other assistant responses while keeping all user messages and a recap, then combine candidates via voting.
fKqAUz2ItR.evidence: Experiments evaluate IC against self-consistency and prior methods across seven white-box and black-box LLMs on synthetically sharded multi-turn tasks.
fKqAUz2ItR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simplicity, training-free black-box applicability, clear presentation, and consistent improvements over self-consistency across seven models.
fKqAUz2ItR.main_concern: Reviewers point out that starting fresh without any assistant history outperforms IC (90 vs. 87) and that matched-K all-assistant-masked baselines are missing, leaving unclear why retaining isolated assistant turns helps.

Q8ai13eyKS.one_liner: Replaces a small fraction of LLM instruction-tuning mixtures with program-generated ground Horn-clause deduction problems and proofs.
Q8ai13eyKS.problem: Synthetic instruction-tuning data typically relies on expensive teacher LLMs, leaving unclear whether purely programmatic symbolic deductions without world knowledge can improve reasoning.
Q8ai13eyKS.method: The authors programmatically generate ground Horn-clause multi-hop deduction problems and checkable derivations over abstract constants with no model in the loop, and substitute 5-25% of an instruction-tuning mixture while holding total example count fixed.
Q8ai13eyKS.key_idea: Replace a small slice of instruction-tuning data with programmatically generated ground Horn-clause deduction traces to instill multi-step derivation habits without a teacher LLM.
Q8ai13eyKS.evidence: Experiments test replacement mixtures on Qwen2.5-7B and five models from three families (3B-14B) across ProofWriter, FOLIO, BIG-Bench Hard, and general benchmarks, with procedural-trace controls.
Q8ai13eyKS.claimed_gains: On Qwen2.5-7B, replacing 5-25% of the mixture raises accuracy by 5 to 16 points on ProofWriter, up to 6 points on FOLIO, and up to 7 points on multi-step BIG-Bench Hard subtasks while leaving general benchmarks mostly unchanged, and 1% suffices for long checker-accepted derivations.
Q8ai13eyKS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that programmatically generated deduction data is a simple, scalable teacher-free intervention with notable gains across multiple reasoning benchmarks and model families.
Q8ai13eyKS.main_concern: Reviewers cite poor organization without a dedicated methodology section, missing code and dataset artifacts for reproducibility, text-table inconsistencies, and weakly motivated baselines and ablations.

7bV0TKbFQd.one_liner: Synthesizes over 18,000 executable hardware-repository training tasks from merged PRs to post-train hardware engineering agents via SFT and RL.
7bV0TKbFQd.problem: Training LLM coding agents for hardware engineering workflows (RTL, simulation, EDA tools) is bottlenecked by scarce public executable interaction environments.
7bV0TKbFQd.method: OriGent mines merged pull requests from 90 public hardware repositories, separates reusable toolchain setups from task construction, builds fail-before/pass-after tests, generates aligned problem statements, and post-trains Qwen3.6-35B-A3B via SFT on teacher trajectories followed by online RL.
7bV0TKbFQd.key_idea: Mine merged hardware-repository PRs into reusable containerized toolchain environments with validated fail-to-pass tests to generate over 18,000 executable tasks for SFT and RL agent post-training.
7bV0TKbFQd.evidence: Experiments train Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 18,000+ synthesized tasks from 90 repositories and evaluate on six held-out HWE-Bench repositories against same-base baselines.
7bV0TKbFQd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that building 18,000+ executable, test-validated tasks across 90 hardware repositories and heterogeneous toolchains is a valuable engineering resource with large gains over same-base baselines.
7bV0TKbFQd.main_concern: Reviewers question whether gains come from hardware-specific environments or teacher distillation from GLM-5.3 (lacking a general-software SFT+RL control), note close similarity to SWE pipelines (R2E-Gym, Scale-SWE), and point out that ~70% of tasks are C/C++ EDA/firmware rather than RTL.

xr3JSU2ls5.one_liner: Fits a training-only principal curve to decompose frozen sequential novelty into progression, transverse deviation, and rate with admissibility gating.
xr3JSU2ls5.problem: Post-hoc novelty detectors collapse representation unusualness into a single scalar, hiding whether anomalies stem from trajectory position, off-manifold deviation, or traversal speed.
xr3JSU2ls5.method: Principal-Curve Novelty Geometry (PCNG) fits a principal curve on training data, checks progression-geometry admissibility, and calibrates progression, transverse deviation, and rate onto a shared rarity scale. It uses targeted interventions and unit-preserving randomization to falsify unsupported interpretations and refuse attribution when geometry fails.
xr3JSU2ls5.key_idea: Project frozen sequential representations onto a training-only principal curve, gate admissibility, calibrate three geometric coordinates by empirical rarity, and test interpretations via interventions and unit-preserving randomization.
xr3JSU2ls5.evidence: Evaluated across 117 degradation-prognostics runs spanning 13 frozen configurations (including PRONOSTIA mentioned in reviews) using failure-mode interventions and cross-unit versus within-unit scrambling.
xr3JSU2ls5.claimed_gains: Failure-mode interventions support the transverse interpretation in 35 of 36 directed tests while rate is unsupported, and cross-unit scrambling reduces transverse hit rate from 0.972 to 0.667 while a within-unit control stays at 1.000.
xr3JSU2ls5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that testing geometric novelty interpretations with falsification controls, reporting negative results, and using unit-preserving randomization for correlated trajectories are valuable.
xr3JSU2ls5.main_concern: Evidence for novelty attribution beyond standard distance-based novelty is narrow, as the 35/36 result relies on non-independent subset pairs and only one coordinate is reliably supported.

8Rdl9qkU1A.one_liner: Evaluates visual reasoning across a seven-rung agent harness ladder from direct answering to persistent code and workspaces.
8Rdl9qkU1A.problem: Existing visual agents couple model, harness, and training choices, obscuring how expanding computational access and workspace delegation affect visual reasoning.
8Rdl9qkU1A.method: The authors define a seven-rung harness ladder progressing from direct answering and fixed visual tools to generated code with a persistent kernel and general workspaces under fixed models and tasks. They construct VHStar, a 600-task benchmark spanning five visual domains and four calibrated difficulty levels.
8Rdl9qkU1A.key_idea: Systematically varies agent harness freedom across seven rungs under fixed models on 600 stratified visual reasoning tasks to isolate environment effects.
8Rdl9qkU1A.evidence: Evaluated nine models across 600 tasks in five domains (integrated from 12 existing datasets), including full-ladder runs, ablations, and token-efficiency analyses.
8Rdl9qkU1A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the systematic harness evaluation protocol and the consistent finding that persistent code execution improves all four full-ladder models over fixed tools.
8Rdl9qkU1A.main_concern: Reviewers warn that workspace-rung drops are confounded by in-house implementation choices (e.g., L6 permission rejections) and single-trajectory runs without repeated rollouts or public harness release.

QF2QUfhGQ0.one_liner: Benchmarks coupled personal-procedural agent memory and trains a memory manager with privileged joint-state supervision.
QF2QUfhGQ0.problem: Agent memory benchmarks treat personal facts and procedural skills separately, overlooking continual maintenance failures when procedures depend on evolving user context.
QF2QUfhGQ0.method: PraxisMemBench evaluates persistent personal assistants across multi-session daily-life and work trajectories where personal and procedural memories co-evolve. PraxisMem trains the memory manager using privileged joint-state supervision (combining location-aware GRPO and residual-routed OPSD) to maintain memory content and organization.
QF2QUfhGQ0.key_idea: Couples evolving personal and procedural memory in a multi-session benchmark and trains a memory manager via privileged joint-state supervision.
QF2QUfhGQ0.evidence: Evaluated on PraxisMemBench across held-out domains and multi-session trajectories, comparing against training-free and learnable memory baselines.
QF2QUfhGQ0.claimed_gains: On PraxisMemBench, baseline completion drops from 84.6% to 77.9% under interdependent memories and relation failures rise from 59.8% to 72.9% from early to late sessions; PraxisMem's numeric gain is not stated in the abstract.
QF2QUfhGQ0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the coupling of personal context and procedural memory as a meaningful, underexplored problem and commend the careful multi-domain benchmark construction.
QF2QUfhGQ0.main_concern: Reviewers note that PraxisMem is trained on the same pipeline and schema as the test split against mostly training-free baselines, uses only eight test trajectories in Table 3, and relies on LLM-generated data and non-strict headline metrics.

kuSAqpyELw.one_liner: Evaluates tool-using agents via deterministic execution replay linking tool calls to authorized, persistent, and transient state transitions.
kuSAqpyELw.problem: Task-success and final-state evaluations miss unauthorized tool-call attempts and transient unauthorized state modifications that disappear before execution ends.
kuSAqpyELw.method: Contract-conditioned intent-state consistency replays reference and agent executions from identical initial states, associates each tool call with realized environment state transitions, and checks tool-call authorization, final-state consistency, and full-trajectory consistency.
kuSAqpyELw.key_idea: Replays agent and reference trajectories from identical initial states to map tool calls to persistent and transient state transitions against an authorization contract.
kuSAqpyELw.evidence: Evaluated across 1,600 replayed AgentDojo trajectories from four models and validated on a stratified human-reviewed sample of 300 trajectories.
kuSAqpyELw.claimed_gains: Full-trajectory evaluation achieves 0.814 precision, 0.809 recall, and 0.811 F1 against human authorization judgments, compared with 0.788 F1 for final-state-only evaluation.
kuSAqpyELw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing failed unauthorized attempts, persistent effects, and transient side effects through state-linked replay and human-labeled validation.
kuSAqpyELw.main_concern: Reviewers note minimal F1 gain from trajectory-action checks (0.809 to 0.816), dependence on externally supplied reference-derived contracts, limited novelty over existing trace checkers like ToolSandbox and AgentPex, and no per-effect-type accuracy breakdown.

EnWBxpAKPd.one_liner: Estimates instance-level rubric completeness via policy perturbations and optimizes worst-case preference loss over completeness-scaled feasible sets.
EnWBxpAKPd.problem: LLM alignment rubrics inevitably omit relevant quality criteria, introducing preference errors even when observed criteria are scored accurately.
EnWBxpAKPd.method: The framework perturbs the policy to generate response variations and measures agreement between response shifts and rubric-score changes as an instance-specific completeness proxy. It then builds a feasible set around observed rubric preference probabilities whose radius scales inversely with estimated completeness and minimizes worst-case preference loss.
EnWBxpAKPd.key_idea: Uses agreement between policy-perturbed response shifts and rubric-score shifts to set instance-level uncertainty radii for worst-case robust preference optimization.
EnWBxpAKPd.evidence: Evaluated across multiple datasets, rubric sources, and margin-aware preference objectives (MMPO, ODPO, Scaled DPO) with Uniform/Shuffled and occlusion ablations.
EnWBxpAKPd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree rubric incompleteness is a practical pain point in alignment and appreciate the plug-and-play robust optimization formulation across multiple objectives.
EnWBxpAKPd.main_concern: Reviewers question whether embedding/response-shift agreement reliably proxies rubric completeness rather than superficial wording or length changes, and note weak theoretical justification for assumption (12) and limited gains over uniform robustness.

1MXE3qQsd7.one_liner: Distills reverse factual knowledge by having frozen teachers score candidates in their known forward direction.
1MXE3qQsd7.problem: LLMs often exhibit the reversal curse, failing to generate reverse relations despite recognizing them, causing students distilled from teacher generations to inherit the failure.
1MXE3qQsd7.method: Directional label distillation uses frozen teachers to score candidate answers in the direction where the teacher's knowledge is accessible, selecting the top-scoring candidate as the student's supervised training target for the reverse query.
1MXE3qQsd7.key_idea: Scores candidate answers with frozen teachers in the known forward direction to construct accurate reverse-query pseudo-labels for student distillation.
1MXE3qQsd7.evidence: Evaluated across multiple teacher and student models on Wikidata parent-child facts, unscreened and two-hop queries, invented facts, and three additional relations.
1MXE3qQsd7.claimed_gains: With evaluated children's forward facts withheld, students gain 13 to 15 points of open-ended accuracy on trained queries over prior-corrected reverse-label training.
1MXE3qQsd7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate distinguishing teacher generation from directional verification as a simple, effective way to produce cleaner distillation targets.
1MXE3qQsd7.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over noisy-channel pseudo-labeling, heavy focus on Wikidata parent-child queries evaluated on trained reverse items, reliance on predefined candidate inventories, and unquantified scoring cost.

87SKGRgDjr.one_liner: Benchmarks uncertainty coverage and latency of CRPS-trained ensembles versus latent and ambient generative emulators on 2D PDEs.
87SKGRgDjr.problem: Uncertainty reliability of probabilistic physical-system emulators—diffusion/flow models versus CRPS-trained ensembles—has not been systematically compared under matched budgets.
87SKGRgDjr.method: The authors build a matched-size, matched-budget evaluation framework across 2D spatiotemporal physical systems, measuring empirical predictive-interval coverage, accuracy, and inference efficiency on single-step forecasts and autoregressive rollouts.
87SKGRgDjr.key_idea: Compares empirical interval coverage, accuracy, and latency of CRPS-trained stochastic ensembles against latent- and ambient-space flow/diffusion models under matched budgets.
87SKGRgDjr.evidence: Empirical study across diverse 64x64 2D spatiotemporal physical systems on single-step prediction and autoregressive rollouts with ablations.
87SKGRgDjr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the clear presentation and balanced empirical comparison of uncertainty coverage between CRPS ensembles and generative emulators.
87SKGRgDjr.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty, small 64x64 deterministic datasets that may not reflect high-dimensional stochastic real-world systems, and confounding from latent-space compression.

Bj9vWccs5l.one_liner: Adapts frozen ECG classifiers to unseen patients using learned multi-slot episodic context memory without test-time labels or gradients.
Bj9vWccs5l.problem: Physiological classifiers trained on short independent windows degrade when deployed on continuous, temporally correlated streams from unseen patients.
Bj9vWccs5l.method: Episodic Context Memory (ECM) freezes a pretrained population ECG classifier and learns shared write and retrieval rules on labeled calibration-patient streams to maintain a compact multi-slot patient memory. At deployment on an unseen patient, only the memory state updates chronologically without labels or gradient steps.
Bj9vWccs5l.key_idea: Learns shared write-and-retrieve rules over calibration patients to update a multi-slot patient context memory for a frozen classifier at deployment.
Bj9vWccs5l.evidence: Evaluated on atrial fibrillation detection across patient-disjoint internal and external ECG cohorts against SFT, test-time adaptation, prototype, recurrent, and neural-memory baselines.
Bj9vWccs5l.claimed_gains: Under external shift, primary ECM increases AUROC by +1.1% and reduces AF burden error by -1.2% over the best comparator; an AF-specific extension raises macro-F1 by +2.7% and AUROC by +2.1%, with up to +15.1% longitudinal macro-F1 gain over the population model.
Bj9vWccs5l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical deployment setting, leak-free chronological evaluation across external cohorts, and broad baseline comparisons.
Bj9vWccs5l.main_concern: Reviewers note reliance on a single non-foundation CNN-Transformer backbone, over one million labeled calibration windows despite 'label-free' terminology, unclear advantage of multi-slot memory over simpler context/LSTM adapters, and dense notation.

MgBOaytxzM.one_liner: Selects Neyman-Pearson classification thresholds in polynomial time across all admissible labelings of selectively labeled data.
MgBOaytxzM.problem: Under selective labeling where prior decisions hide outcomes for unselected instances, standard Neyman-Pearson classifiers cannot reliably control population type I error.
MgBOaytxzM.method: NPSL encodes structural assumptions on unlabeled class proportions and score distributions into an admissible labeling set. Given an independently trained scoring function, it exploits cumulative monotonicity to compute the worst-case empirical type I error across exponentially many labelings in polynomial time and choose a robust threshold.
MgBOaytxzM.key_idea: Exploits monotone cumulative structure to compute exact worst-case empirical type I error over an admissible labeling set in polynomial time for Neyman-Pearson thresholding.
MgBOaytxzM.evidence: Provides asymptotic convergence theory alongside synthetic selective-labeling experiments and real-world LendingClub evaluations.
MgBOaytxzM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the polynomial-time exact worst-case risk computation and clear formulation of selective-label Neyman-Pearson risk control.
MgBOaytxzM.main_concern: Reviewers criticize strong, unverifiable structural assumptions on unlabeled data and a theoretical gap between fixed-set convergence guarantees and data-dependent default calibration limits.

jMFbdAu8wH.one_liner: Defends LLMs against multi-turn jailbreaks by replacing unsafe drafts with preference-optimized non-actionable decoy responses.
jMFbdAu8wH.problem: Standard safety refusals expose boundary feedback that multi-turn jailbreak attackers exploit to iteratively adapt their prompts.
jMFbdAu8wH.method: META-TRAP defines a taxonomy of deception strategies, trains a meta-cognitive planner via misDirection Preference Optimization (DePO) contrasting optimal interventions against under-protective and over-aggressive alternatives, and uses a strategy-conditioned misdirection agent to rewrite unsafe drafts into plausible non-actionable decoys.
jMFbdAu8wH.key_idea: Trains a dialogue-state planner with DePO to invoke a separate agent that replaces unsafe drafts with strategy-conditioned non-actionable decoy responses.
jMFbdAu8wH.evidence: Evaluated across three target LLMs (including GPT-4.1 and open-source models), three multi-turn jailbreak attacks, HarmBench, Malicious-Educator, and utility benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K).
jMFbdAu8wH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize interactive active defense as an interesting perspective and note substantial attack-success-rate reductions while preserving benign utility.
jMFbdAu8wH.main_concern: Reviewers point out the lack of a matched non-deceptive rewrite control to isolate deception from draft replacement, missing comparisons to prior decoy defenses (e.g., HoneyTrap), and limited novelty in DePO over standard DPO.

bGtEjuKJuB.one_liner: Exchanges bidirectional answer-prefix KV caches to localize latent-to-prefix answer relays in latent-reasoning models.
bGtEjuKJuB.problem: Latent-reasoning models can emit identical answer prefixes after different latent computations yet produce different answers, leaving the readout pathway unclear.
bGtEjuKJuB.method: Boundary-Resolved Answer Transport and Sensitivity (BATS) exchanges contextual prefix caches bidirectionally across latent backgrounds, recomputes the terminal reader, and separately measures destructive sensitivity to localize writer, prefix-value, and terminal-reader pathways.
bGtEjuKJuB.key_idea: Performs bidirectional prefix-cache interchange and destructive-sensitivity ablation to isolate how latent states write answers into answer-prefix values read by terminal heads.
bGtEjuKJuB.evidence: Evaluated on CODI-GPT-2 (64 held-out arithmetic pairs with eight fixed reader heads) and a frozen SIM-CoT 8B readout on arithmetic word problems.
bGtEjuKJuB.claimed_gains: Exchanging prefix values across eight fixed reader heads transfers the donor answer on 61/64 new arithmetic pairs, and restoring clean values recovers the recipient answer on all 64 under greedy decoding.
bGtEjuKJuB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the four-condition bidirectional cache-interchange design separating donor transfer from destructive disruption and the fixed-mechanism held-out confirmation.
bGtEjuKJuB.main_concern: Reviewers note limited generalization beyond one small CODI-GPT-2 checkpoint on templated arithmetic, intervention-dependent localization, and whether prefix-KV answer storage is specific to latent reasoning.

9U7KAv1pIa.one_liner: Amortizes cooperative-game Myerson node values and conditional edge gains into a sparse multi-agent LLM communication policy.
9U7KAv1pIa.problem: Extra communication in multi-agent LLM reasoning increases token cost and can propagate incorrect rationales into false consensus.
9U7KAv1pIa.method: GAMMA models agents as players in a graph-restricted cooperative game, computes offline supervision from node-level Myerson contributions and cost-aware conditional edge values, and trains a lightweight graph policy for sparse message routing and contribution-weighted aggregation.
9U7KAv1pIa.key_idea: Amortizes offline graph-restricted Myerson node contributions and conditional edge values into a lightweight policy for sparse multi-agent routing and weighted aggregation.
9U7KAv1pIa.evidence: Evaluated on nine reasoning benchmarks using Qwen3.5-9B with ablation, calibration, error-propagation, and token-usage analyses.
9U7KAv1pIa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate separately modeling agent contributions and marginal message value via cooperative game theory and the broad nine-benchmark evaluation.
9U7KAv1pIa.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing offline label-generation cost accounting, evaluation restricted to one model (Qwen3.5-9B), unclear token accounting versus majority vote, and a gap between graph-conditioned edge targets and one-shot online edge selection.

AaMe97lhm1.one_liner: Curates robot demonstrations via consensus trajectory-efficiency rankings from lightweight progress predictors trained on random subsets.
AaMe97lhm1.problem: Curating robot imitation-learning demonstrations is expensive or infeasible when trusted reference demonstrations and online policy rollouts are unavailable.
AaMe97lhm1.method: Trajectory Progress Efficiency Consensus (TPEC) samples small uncurated reference sets directly from the candidate dataset, trains lightweight timestamp-based progress predictors, and aggregates whole-trajectory efficiency scores into a consensus ranking to select action chunks.
AaMe97lhm1.key_idea: Trains lightweight progress predictors on small random in-dataset reference subsets and aggregates whole-trajectory efficiency scores into a consensus ranking for action-chunk selection.
AaMe97lhm1.evidence: Evaluated on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboMimic, and real-robot tasks including joint fine-tuning of the billion-parameter VLA model pi0, plus curation-time benchmarks against CUPID and WARP-RM.
AaMe97lhm1.claimed_gains: Matches or exceeds full-data fine-tuning of pi0 using 50% of action chunks, with curation-preparation speedups of 2,257x over CUPID and 4.53x over WARP-RM.
AaMe97lhm1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the low-cost, rollout-free curation framing without curated reference demonstrations and the large preparation-time speedup over gradient-based methods.
AaMe97lhm1.main_concern: Reviewers find weak performance advantages over random selection and simple shortest-trajectory heuristics, unsubstantiated large-scale pretraining claims, and sensitivity to low-quality random reference subsets.

zEYuYszpie.one_liner: Studies RL with biased verifiers on text arithmetic and shows hidden reward-hacking susceptibility persists after supervised repair.
zEYuYszpie.problem: Practical verifiers used in LLM post-training contain systematic biases, and it is unclear what hidden vulnerabilities they leave in trained models or pass to distilled students.
zEYuYszpie.method: The authors run RL on text arithmetic with an imperfect verifier that also rewards wrong answers containing a marker token (such as python), then test whether susceptibility to collapse persists after fine-tuning repair and whether it transfers through filtered teacher-student distillation.
zEYuYszpie.key_idea: Measure latent reward-hacking susceptibility via repeated RL runs under a marker-biased verifier before and after supervised accuracy repair and student distillation.
zEYuYszpie.evidence: Evaluated with 10 to 40 RL seeds per arm, Wilson 95% confidence intervals, Fisher's exact tests, and an independent lineage rerun on arithmetic tasks.
zEYuYszpie.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the statistical rigor across many RL seeds and the repair experiment showing that equally accurate checkpoints can hide very different collapse risks.
zEYuYszpie.main_concern: Reviewers criticize pseudoreplication with only one or two independent base checkpoints per arm and argue that broader persistence and non-transmission claims exceed the narrow experimental scope.

y8rcOdU497.one_liner: Combines plan-conditioned on-device visual tools with alignment-gated asynchronous prefetching during cloud planning for GUI agents.
y8rcOdU497.problem: Rigid one-way handoffs in device-cloud GUI agents force sequential grounding after cloud responses and leave on-device compute idle during cloud reasoning, hurting accuracy and latency.
y8rcOdU497.method: TAP-Agent runs plan-conditioned visual experts after each cloud response to compile semantic-geometric action representations, while using a compact experience buffer during cloud wait intervals to prefetch likely visual evidence. An alignment check reuses matching prefetched outputs while keeping UI-changing actions gated on confirmed cloud instructions.
y8rcOdU497.key_idea: Speculatively prefetch visual grounding on-device during cloud planning using a verified experience buffer and reuse results only when aligned with the confirmed cloud plan.
y8rcOdU497.evidence: Evaluated on AndroidWorld and OSWorld across four on-device executor model sizes against EcoAgent and a fully-cloud upper bound.
y8rcOdU497.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing cloud waiting time as schedulable compute for alignment-gated speculative prefetching is well-motivated and reduces local latency safely.
y8rcOdU497.main_concern: Reviewers point out that nearly all success-rate gains come from existing post-response visual tools rather than prefetching, baselines omit closest idle-precomputation work, and on-device memory cost is impractical for phones.

JcIG5NkCvk.one_liner: Pre-trains a unified Population Transformer on scalp EEG and iEEG using frozen channel tokens and spherical-coordinate positional encodings.
JcIG5NkCvk.problem: Whether adding intracranial EEG to scalp-EEG foundation model pre-training improves decoding has not been cleanly isolated in a coordinate-aware architecture.
JcIG5NkCvk.method: UniPopT encodes every scalp and intracranial electrode with a frozen single-channel encoder, tags tokens with spherical-coordinate and modality positional encodings, and pre-trains a shared aggregator with next-segment and replaced-token objectives. Controlled ablations separate encoder-bank, aggregator-corpus, and positional-encoding effects.
JcIG5NkCvk.key_idea: Map scalp EEG and iEEG channels into a shared transformer aggregator using frozen single-channel tokens and spherical-coordinate plus modality positional encodings.
JcIG5NkCvk.evidence: Evaluated on official splits of two clinical EEG corpora (including TUAB and TUEV) and external scalp-EEG and iEEG leaderboards on Brain4FMs with five-variant equal-compute ablations.
JcIG5NkCvk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the disciplined equal-compute ablation study localizing gains to the aggregator corpus and the competitive scalp-EEG fine-tuning performance.
JcIG5NkCvk.main_concern: Reviewers argue that the headline claim of iEEG helping scalp EEG is confounded by a 31% larger bimodal pre-training corpus (4,043 vs. 3,076 recordings) and that iEEG evaluation is limited to two seizure tasks.
